title: ‘X-Files’ star Gillian Anderson reveals parenting regret, says she wishes she was 'less selfish'
summary: Gillian Anderson reveals she wishes she'd been "less selfish" in early parenting while filming "The X-Files" and working grueling 17-hour days.
story: "Chrisley Knows Best" stars Todd and Julie Chrisley explained how their approaches to parenting changed since their time in prison.
Gillian Anderson is looking back at the sacrifices she made as her Hollywood career took off — and acknowledging that some of those choices came at a cost for her family.

In a new interview with The Sunday Times, the 58-year-old actress — who became a household name playing FBI Special Agent Dana Scully on "The X-Files" — opened up about her regrets as a young mother and explained how the show’s grueling production schedule affected her ability to be present for her daughter.

"I have absolutely no regrets in my life," Anderson initially told the outlet before reconsidering. "No, there are a couple of things, in terms of early parenting, that I now would say, I wish I’d thought this through or I wish I’d been less selfish."
SCARLETT JOHANSSON, WHO EARNED $43 MILLION IN 2025, SAYS LIFE IS A CONSTANT 'DEFICIT' AT HOME
Gillian Anderson said she regrets working so much when her daughter was a young child. (Getty Images)
Anderson became a mother at 26, welcoming daughter Piper with her first husband, "The X-Files" assistant art director Clyde Klotz, just over a year after she began filming the hit Fox sci-fi series.
Her career was rapidly accelerating at the time, with "The X-Files" becoming a global phenomenon and Anderson facing grueling days on set.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
After Anderson and Klotz divorced in 1997, Piper split her time between her mother, who was working on "The X-Files" in Los Angeles, and her father in Vancouver.
OLIVIA WILDE SPEAKS OUT ABOUT THE EXACT MOMENT SHE KNEW RELATIONSHIP WITH JASON SUDEIKIS WAS OVER

In an effort to maintain consistency in her daughter's education, Piper attended a French lycée in both cities. The arrangement, however, meant the young girl was regularly traveling between her parents.
Anderson is mom to three children. (Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images)
"It was intense for her, with no French in the household, to suddenly be getting a plane every three weeks," Anderson recalled. "It’s a lot to ask of a six-year-old."

The actress said she was working 17-hour days and didn't believe she was in a position to push back against the demanding schedule, despite being one of the show's two central stars alongside David Duchovny.
TOM SELLECK SAYS 'BLUE BLOODS' CAST MADE MAJOR SACRIFICE TO SAVE SHOW BEFORE CANCELLATION
"That show couldn’t have done without [me], and so I had leverage that I’m not sure I knew," Anderson said.
Anderson has previously spoken about wondering whether she could have made different choices as a working mother.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

In a previous interview with The Sunday Times, the actress acknowledged there was another version of her life in which she could have worked less, lived on a smaller scale and been more present for her children.
Gillian Anderson starred as FBI Special Agent Dana Scully on "The X-Files" opposite David Duchovny, who played FBI Special Agent Fox Mulder, from 1993 to 2002. (Getty Images)

"There's another version of my life where I could have worked less, had a smaller life and been more present as a parent. I could have chosen that, that could happen," she said. "But sometimes it feels like why would you, if you keep getting work as an actor, doing things you dreamt of doing and being offered incredible roles at this age, while paying the bills, and you still get to see them a huge percentage of the time and they witness a mother enjoying her work?
Her approach to parenting changed when she later welcomed sons Oscar and Felix with businessman Mark Griffiths.
GOLDIE HAWN SOUNDS THE ALARM ON CHILDHOOD CELEBRITY CULTURE: 'ALL I CAN SAY IS IT'S A NIGHTMARE'
Despite reflecting on what she might have done differently, Anderson has continued working steadily decades after "The X-Files" made her famous.
The actress turned 58 on Aug. 9. (Getty Images)
HEATHER GRAHAM SAYS CLASSMATES DISMISSED HER AS 'NERDY' BEFORE HOLLYWOOD BREAKTHROUGH PROVED THEM WRONG

Her more recent credits include "The Crown," "Sex Education" and "The Salt Path." She also stars opposite Hannah Einbinder in filmmaker Jane Schoenbrun’s "Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma," which premiered at the Cannes Film Festival.
Anderson suggested that her relationship with work remains complicated as she approaches 60.
"I feel very lucky to still be working," she told The Sunday Times, adding that while she once imagined slowing down in her 60s to direct and make art, she is reconsidering those plans.

"I’m having so much fun," she said.

title: Chrissy Metz slams weight loss critics, says they're always 'going to have something to say'
summary: Chrissy Metz slams online critics commenting on her body and reveals how her father's death from obesity complications led her to start GLP-1 medication.
story: Chrissy Metz tells Fox News Digital she was the middle child of five.
Chrissy Metz is firing back at the haters commenting on her weight loss.
During a recent appearance on "The Tamsen Show" podcast, the 45-year-old actress spoke about why she chose to start taking a GLP-1 medication and slammed haters who comment on her body.

"It's not that I don't have people and naysayers and people who comment all kinds of stuff still to this day," she said. "Like I don't know when people will stop doing that. I don't think it ever will happen."
She then recalled a recent incident in which a distant relative congratulated her for "taking control of your weight," as "weight has always been an issue in our family."
Metz shared internet trolls will always have something to say. (Raymond Hall/GC Images)
JACK OSBOURNE FIRES BACK AT BODY SHAMERS CALLING HIM 'GROSSLY UNDERWEIGHT'

Metz explained that the relative is "an overweight woman" herself, so she understands the struggles of living in the world as an overweight person. She said comments about her weight from the relative don't sting as much, but added, "The other comments are a little…it's wild to me."

"It's interesting what people say cause would they ever say it to you on the streets? Never. Never," she explained. "They're like, 'Oh, Chrissy, you're pretty, but them eyebrows.' I'm like, 'Oh my god, it doesn't matter what I do. It doesn't matter.'"
She then shared some of the types of comments she received, including "Why'd you wear that? Why did you do this? Like why aren't you losing weight? Oh, you're losing weight?"

"It doesn't matter. It doesn't matter what you do," Metz said. "And I know it's not personal, but it can be taxing, but you sometimes just got to just shut it off cuz no matter what you do, somebody's going to have something to say."
Metz is currently starring in the Broadway musical, "& Juliet." (Getty Images for A+E Global Media)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Metz, who is currently starring in the Broadway musical "& Juliet," called receiving all the criticism and "still doing what you want to do...an act of rebellion."
The "This Is Us" actress also discussed her use of a GLP-1 medication this week during an appearance on "Today."

She told the podcast host that she was always "skeptical" of GLP-1s and that it was something she "was so afraid of even sort of partaking in," but her mentality changed when her father "unfortunately passed away from obesity complications."
One of the ways in which the medication helped her was by quieting the food noise in her mind, which she described as being "loud."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Metz said the GLP-1 has helped her quiet the food noise. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)

"I know it sounds so silly now, but I'm like, 'Oh, not everybody hears that all the time? Oh, okay. Oh, there's like something chemically off and metabolically off and hereditary, you know, issues,'" she said. "And so really when that happened with my family and my father, I was like, I have to do something about it. And so, yeah...I feel better on the medication."
The actress is now partnering with Ro, a telehealth company that provides medications for a number of issues, including weight loss.

title: Kelly Clarkson won’t let her kids watch ‘From Justin to Kelly’ after brutal admission about 2003 film
summary: Kelly Clarkson revealed at her final Las Vegas concert that she has banned her children from watching "From Justin to Kelly," calling it bluntly terrible.
story: Kate Hudson told Fox News Digital that she is actively trying not to raise fame-obsessed children.
Kelly Clarkson has no plans to introduce her children to one infamous chapter of her career.

During her final Las Vegas concert on Saturday, the 44-year-old singer revealed that she has banned daughter River Rose, 12, and son Remington, 10, from watching her 2003 musical comedy, "From Justin to Kelly."

"Well, it’s an Oscar-worthy number, and it’s called ‘From Justin to Kelly,’" Clarkson joked, according to a video obtained by Us Weekly, before explaining her participation in two words: "Contractually obligated."
KELLY CLARKSON LAUGHS OFF WIND-BLOWN WARDROBE MALFUNCTION ON STAGE
Kelly Clarkson and Justin Guarini co-starred in the 2003 musical comedy, "From Justin to Kelly." (Getty Images)

"Man, read the f—ing fine print, you know," she told the crowd. "I didn’t know that if you won, you had to do a movie. Not all of us want to be Meryl Streep, we just like watching her, OK? I was like, ‘I don’t want to be in a movie,’ but they were like, ‘Yeah, but you won.’ And I was like, ‘And I feel like I’m losing? It doesn’t feel quite like a win.’"
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Clarkson starred opposite "American Idol" season one runner-up Justin Guarini in the musical, which hit theaters shortly after she became the reality competition’s inaugural winner. The movie followed two young people who meet and fall for each other while on spring break.
Clarkson, who won the first season of "American Idol," said the movie she made with runner-up Guarini was "s---." (SGranitz/WireImage/Getty Images)
More than two decades later, Clarkson made clear she isn't looking back at the project through rose-colored glasses.
After a fan at the concert defended the film, Clarkson joked that the audience member was watching it with "loving eyes," before offering her own decidedly less flattering assessment: "It’s s---."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
And her two children apparently won't get the chance to judge her performance for themselves anytime soon.
"It is funny though, like, my kids, I’ve banned them from watching," Clarkson admitted.
Clarkson said she was "contractually obligated" to make the film after winning the first season. (Kevin Winter/ImageDirect)
Despite her feelings about the film, the singer said the experience wasn't entirely negative.
"The music part, that was fun," she said. "See? You gotta find the positive, motherf—ers, you know? Turn that s— into lemonade … and cry yourself to sleep."

"From Justin to Kelly" was released in 2003, one year after Clarkson's victory on the first season of "American Idol."

title: ‘American Pie’ star Shannon Elizabeth swears off dating, says OnlyFans is ‘the only relationship I need’
summary: Shannon Elizabeth told Bill Maher on "Club Random" that OnlyFans is "the only relationship I need" after swearing off dating following her divorce.
story: Shannon Elizabeth opens up about joining OnlyFans, exploring boundaries and finding empowerment during a major life transition.
Shannon Elizabeth isn’t looking for another slice of romance anytime soon.
The "American Pie" star, whose divorce was finalized in May, has sworn off dating, insisting that OnlyFans is "the only relationship I need."
During an appearance on Bill Maher's "Club Random" podcast, he asked her, "What’s the dating scene like in Cape Town?" Elizabeth moved to South Africa in 2016 to focus on wildlife conservation.
‘AMERICAN PIE’ ALUM SHANNON ELIZABETH TURNS TO ONLYFANS FOR ‘FRESH START’ AS DIVORCE UNFOLDS
In May, actress Shannon Elizabeth spoke to Fox News Digital about her decision to join OnlyFans and how fun it's been for her. (Jonathan Leibson/Getty Images for Patron)
"I'm very newly single, and I don’t plan on ever dating again, to be honest," Elizabeth replied.
"Come on, you’re going to date," Maher insisted.
"No, no," Elizabeth said.
"No, not even dating?" Maher said.
WATCH: ‘AMERICAN PIE’ STAR LAUNCHES ONLYFANS, EMBRACES FRESH START
"I do not want to date," Elizabeth said. "I’m not interested. There’s too many con artists out there. There’s too many people I don’t trust. I have no interest."
"... The only relationships I need are the relationships on OnlyFans that I’m building with all of these people," Elizabeth said.
Maher was adamant that Elizabeth’s ban on dating wouldn’t stick.
Comedian and television host Bill Maher spoke to Shannon Elizabeth on his podcast "Club Random with Bill Maher." (Alex Wroblewski/AFP via Getty Images)
"Well, I’m not saying I know you better than you, because I don’t," he said. "You know you better than you. I will say this: I have heard that from many people right after. ..."
"I mean, including many celebrities," he said.

Maher pointed to Halle Berry as an example, noting that the actress had once said she would never marry again. Berry later married actor Olivier Martinez in 2013, and the couple filed for divorce in 2015.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Halle Berry and Olivier Martinez married on July 13, 2013, in France. They announced their separation and filed for divorce in October 2015. They were declared legally single in December 2016, and their divorce settlement was finalized in August 2023. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images)
Elizabeth wasn't swayed.
"... At the moment, I’m perfectly fine not being with anyone and not wanting anything," she said.

OnlyFans allows creators to charge fans directly for their content, and Elizabeth found immediate financial success on the subscription platform. Variety reported that she earned more than $1.2 million in her first week after launching her account in April.
Shannon Elizabeth is interviewed by Jay Leno on "The Tonight Show" on Aug. 23, 2001. (Paul Drinkwater/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal)

For Elizabeth, however, OnlyFans has become more than another source of income. She told Variety the platform provided a financial lifeline as she went through her divorce from Simon Borchert. Acting roles weren't coming in as frequently as they once did, she said, and she had largely been living off her savings.

"For the last ten years, I’ve been living off of my savings for the most part, because I haven’t been as focused on work," she said. "To be able to get myself back to the point where I’m not struggling and am able to choose projects because I like them and not because I need the money — it’s definitely giving me more freedom to do that."
WATCH: SHANNON ELIZABETH REFLECTS ON ‘AMERICAN PIE’ AND NEW MISSION
Elizabeth also wants to direct and "be behind the camera." In the meantime, she’s directing and producing her OnlyFans content, which does not currently include nudity.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Shannon Elizabeth, who starred in 1999's "American Pie," has moved to South Africa where she launched the Shannon Elizabeth Foundation to help wildlife in need. (Cliff Lipson/CBS via Getty Images)

"I’ve got to be a little bit mysterious," she said. "I do all kinds of content, but I don’t even know what my boundaries will be. I’m still exploring it, and as I become more comfortable with it, I’m going to push those boundaries."
A portion of Elizabeth’s OnlyFans earnings goes to her wildlife conservation nonprofit.
Elizabeth previously told Fox News Digital that she isn't worried about criticism of her latest venture.
Shannon Elizabeth played Nadia, Jim’s foreign exchange student crush, in "American Pie" (1999). (Getty Images)

"I know people do make assumptions about creators on the platform," she said. "But I don’t go looking for it. And people have been nothing but really supportive and kind to me. ... I’m really happy doing it. I’m really having so much fun. I’m connecting with people. And I think no matter what you do in any industry, there’s always going to be people who don’t support you, who want to bring you down or who criticize you."
One piece of advice Elizabeth would give to another actress considering OnlyFans is simple: Just do it.

"Absolutely do it," she gushed. "It’s been an incredible experience. And if you don’t like it, you just stop. That’s the beauty of it. The control’s in your hands. So if you want to do it for one month, do it for a month. See if you like it. In fact, I have already started talking to some friends about getting on the platform with me, and a lot of people are starting to consider it."
Shannon Elizabeth at the 33rd Annual EMA Awards Gala held at Sunset Las Palmas Studios on Jan. 27, 2024, in Los Angeles. (Christopher Polk/Variety via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"[This is] something that we wanted to do 25 years ago, but the technology wasn’t there yet," she said. "Now the technology is there. I just wish I’d done it sooner."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Amanda Kloots confronts biggest misconception about dating after losing a spouse
summary: Amanda Kloots tells Fox News Digital dating after losing Nick Cordero to COVID-19 doesn't mean loving him any less, revealing the misconception widows face most.
story: The "Good Grief" podcast host tells Fox News Digital losing a spouse doesn't close the door to love, sharing why widows and widowers can embrace new relationships.
Amanda Kloots is challenging a common misconception about dating after losing a spouse — that moving forward means leaving the person you lost behind.

Kloots, who lost her husband, Broadway star Nick Cordero, to COVID-19 in 2020, said widows and widowers can face judgment when they begin opening their hearts to someone new — even though grief and love don't simply disappear when a new relationship begins.
AMANDA KLOOTS HONORS LATE HUSBAND NICK CORDERO IN NEW MEMOIR, SAYS HE ‘TRULY JUST LOVED LIFE’
Amanda Kloots opens up about feeling spiritually connected to Nick Cordero six years after his death while embracing new love and relationships. (Jason Armond/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

"The heart can hold a lot of love," Kloots said in an interview with Fox News Digital. "And just because I'm dating again or any widow or widower is dating again, it doesn't mean that you don't love your person that you lost still or any less."
"It’s in fact more," the "Good Grief" podcast host shared.
Kloots isn't asking people to believe that grief disappears.
She's asking them to acknowledge that it doesn't have to prevent someone from living.
AMANDA KLOOTS SHARES 'HUGE MEDICAL BILL' FROM NICK CORDERO'S HOSPITAL STAY, VENTILATOR COST $3,000 DAILY
The "Good Grief" podcast host shares how her heart holds space for Nick Cordero and new love, urging people to support widows. (Phillip Faraone/Getty Images)

"I have many compartments in my heart for love and new relationships," she said. "It's like having more children. It doesn't mean you… love your child less… now [that] you have a new child. Your heart is able to hold many, many types of love, and I wish people understood that you can hold those two things very close."
She said new love does not erase old love.
And for anyone who dates a widow or widower, Kloots explained that reality needs to be understood from the start.
WATCH: AMANDA KLOOTS DEFENDS DATING AGAIN AFTER HUSBAND NICK CORDERO'S DEATH
"These people are never leaving our lives, but there's definitely room and space for new love, new relationships, new marriage and it's so beautiful."
"Celebrate and help and support friends in your life who are on this journey," she said. "It is so difficult and it is so hard and if you make it harder for us, it really isn't fair."
Amanda Kloots challenges the misconception about widows dating, saying grief and new love can coexist. (Jim Spellman/WireImage)

"So really support those people and guide them along on this because they're doing something that is something they never wish they had to do," she continued. "It's not, they're not dating again because ‘yay!’ It's a different type of dating again. So, support them, love them, be kind."

Cordero died on July 5, 2020, after spending 95 days in the hospital battling COVID-19. The Broadway star endured mini-strokes, blood clots, septic infections and a tracheostomy before doctors amputated his right leg.

Kloots documented his fight for his life publicly, giving followers a front-row seat to a nightmare that began just as she, Cordero and their then-9-month-old son, Elvis, were starting a new life in Los Angeles.
They had moved from New York City in March 2020, chasing what was supposed to be a dream.
Kloots suddenly became a widow — and she's never stopped talking about Cordero.
WATCH: AMANDA KLOOTS SHARES HOW SHE STILL FEELS LATE HUSBAND NICK CORDERO'S PRESENCE
She believes stopping the conversation is one of the biggest mistakes people make after someone dies.

"If he was still alive, I'd be talking about him all the time. He's still in my life. I have a son that I'm raising that's his, and I need to make sure that Elvis knows who his dad was and that the world never forgets him."
Cordero, she said, "was such a beautiful man."
Amanda Kloots urges others to keep talking about their loved ones after they're gone. (Walter McBride/WireImage)

"And I don't think anyone we lose has to be forgotten forever," she continued. "Keep saying their names, keep talking about them, keep celebrating them, celebrate their birthdays, celebrate their anniversaries, honor them at the holidays, and every day. They can still be around."
For Kloots, Cordero's presence isn't simply a metaphor. She says she has continued to feel spiritually connected to him since his death.
"You know, they mean everything," Kloots said of the signs she believes she receives from him.

"I feel like when you lose somebody there's such a finality with death, and you really feel like there's no way you'll ever connect with them again, of course. And I started asking for signs right away from Nick, and he started showing up and I just kind of really went all in on it..."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I do feel like he's around Elvis and I all the time, and we get signs all the time from him, and I feel like he's on my spirit team just guiding us every single day, and I do feel this really beautiful spiritual connection with him that has got me through these last six years."
Amanda Kloots in episode 101 of Netflix's "Let's Marry Harry." (Netflix)
That perspective has followed Kloots into her newest chapter — including her role on Netflix's "Let's Marry Harry."
The show puts reality star and notorious bachelor Harry Jowsey's dating life in the hands of three trusted friends, with Kloots serving as a big-sister-like confidante.
WATCH: AMANDA KLOOTS AND REALITY STAR HARRY JOWSEY TOOK 'FULL INVENTORY' OF HIS DATING LIFE BEFORE 'LET'S MARRY HARRY'
Before filming began, she and Jowsey spent time talking about love, marriage and relationships.
"I told him constantly, you know, how you love is so important and marriage changes over time. And you have to really love and communicate with your partner."
Amanda Kloots officiated Harry Jowsey's wedding on the Netflix show. (Netflix)
Kloots said she quickly noticed a pattern in Jowsey's romantic history.
"He had kind of a track record of fighting equaled love for him."
She challenged him to rethink it.
"What if we flip the switch here? Because I've learned, you know, that I shouldn't have fought so much with my partner. I would take them all back now. I don't have him around anymore."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Kloots emphasized to Fox News Digital that she isn’t romanticizing loss but learning from it.
Amanda Kloots launched her podcast "Good Grief with Amanda Kloots." (Amanda Kloots)
She's turning that experience into "Good Grief with Amanda Kloots," her new podcast.
The show tackles grief in its many forms, from death and divorce to lost careers, relationships, identities and futures people thought they were guaranteed to have.
Kloots' grief doesn't have an expiration date, and neither does love.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Six years after Cordero's death, she is still carrying him with her while making room for the life ahead.
Stephanie Giang-Paunon is an entertainment reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: What Taylor Sheridan's biggest stars really think about working with the 'Yellowstone' creator
summary: Zoe Saldaña, Billy Bob Thornton, Harrison Ford and Kevin Costner reveal what it's really like working with Taylor Sheridan on his hit shows.
story: Billy Bob Thornton told Fox News Digital that Taylor Sheridan's "Landman" is a worldwide phenomenon.
The third season of Taylor Sheridan's hit show "Lioness" has officially begun.

"Lioness" is one of many successful shows created by the prolific TV writer and showrunner. His long list of credits also include "Yellowstone," "1923," "Landman," "The Madison" and many other popular shows.
It's not only audiences who have fallen in love with the complex characters and storylines Sheridan has created, but also the actors who work on his sets.
Here is what some of his stars have said about what it's really like to work with Sheridan.
ZOE SALDANA SAYS TAYLOR SHERIDAN GIVES STARS TWO CHOICES: 'MAKE SURE THAT YOU DON'T F--K UP... OR YOU QUIT'
Sheridan's actors have all spoken about his abilities as a writer. (Omar Vega/Getty Images)
Michael Kelly
Kelly called Sheridan "one of the greatest storytellers in history." (TheStewartofNY/FilmMagic)
Ahead of the season three premiere of "Lioness," one of its stars, Michael Kelly, told People that Sheridan is "truly a standalone talent."
"There’s nobody who’s doing or has ever done what he’s doing," he said. "It’s incredible what he does. And he’s just one of the smartest dudes you’ll ever meet."
He added, "He’s f---ing brilliant, man. Brilliant. And just one of the greatest storytellers."

When it comes to working with the showrunner in the future, Kelly said that while he's "never thought about how the shows could cross over," he has told Sheridan, "anything you want me to do, I'll do."
He told Sheridan, "I love being in Texas. I love saying your words," and, "Anything, dude. You can put me in. Put me in, coach. Wherever you want to put me, I’ll go."
Zoe Saldaña

Zoe Saldaña opened up about working with Taylor Sheridan, saying the "Lioness" creator challenges actors while remaining collaborative on set. (Dia Dipasupil/WireImage/Getty Images; Phillip Faraone/Getty Images for Viacom/Getty Images)

Actress Zoe Saldaña has starred in all three seasons of "Lioness," and told "CBS Mornings" that while she can "feel like an old soldier" on set, when Sheridan shows he believes in her, "you have no other choice but to start believing in yourself again."
The actress also referred to him as "an intimidating cat," who comes to set ready and "so serious," noting, "it raises the bar for the rest of us."

"So working with him is a challenge in the sense that he does raise the bar," Saldaña also told People. "And you have one of two choices. You either accept the challenge and make sure that you don't f--- up... or you quit."
Zoe Saldaña plays the role of Joe in "Lioness." (Lauren Smith/Paramount+)

She added that one of the benefits of working with Sheridan is that "he's an incredibly smart person" who puts in a ton of research when writing his scripts, "And then he writes these incredibly elaborate shows that end up really educating us as well."
"It's actually great," she added. "When you work with him is when you realize how passionate he is about actors and about acting. I think it is his first love when it comes to the arts."
Billy Bob Thornton
Thornton said he loves working with Sheridan on "Landman." (Scott Dudelson/Getty Images for Stagecoach)
When speaking at a Q&A in Hollywood in April, "Landman" star Billy Bob Thornton told the crowd that he has a lot of trust in the show, noting, "I trust Taylor and I trust the castmates."
"Yeah, oh, it’s great. I love working with Taylor," Thornton said, per People. "I love hanging out with him after hours. He’s such a brilliant guy, great writer, and I love his company."
Michelle Pfeiffer
Pfeiffer checked with Helen Mirren before accepting the role in Sheridan's show, "The Madison." (Steve Granitz/FilmMagic)
When speaking with The Hollywood Reporter in March, Michelle Pfeiffer spoke about how Sheridan convinced her to star in "The Madison."

"[Taylor] wanted to know who Stacy was before he started writing. I wanted to know who Stacy is before I committed. And so we went back and forth like that for a little while, and it became clear to me I wasn’t going to win this battle," Pfeiffer said. "So I asked Helen Mirren [who previously starred in Sheridan's "Yellowstone" spinoff "1923"] to speak to me about her experience."

"And she just glowed; she couldn’t say enough nice things," Pfeiffer recalled of Mirren. "She said the scripts were great, the productions were perfect. She was having the time of her life; she loved Montana. So I took a big leap of faith, and I committed. I thought, 'Well, the guy has a pretty darn good track record.'"
Harrison Ford
Ford called Sheridan an incredible writer and an intellectual. (John Sciulli/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images)

Harrison Ford starred in Sheridan's "Yellowstone" prequel series, "1923," and had nothing but nice things to say about the showrunner when speaking about him at the premiere of the show in December 2022.
"He’s an incredible horseman. He’s a genuine athlete, and that’s something you might not expect to find in such a talented writer and intellectual thinker," he told The Hollywood Reporter.
Kevin Costner
Costner told Entertainment Weekly that Sheridan is "doing special work." (Getty Images)

Ahead of the release of his movie "Horizon: An American Saga" in 2024, Kevin Costner spoke with Entertainment Weekly about working with Sheridan, as his future on "Yellowstone" was uncertain at the time.
The actor told the outlet that Sheridan is "doing special work in a lot of different ways."

"He's very prolific about the things he does, and if he sees me in something that he wants to do, I'll look at it just the way I did 'Yellowstone' and maybe we will end up doing something together," Costner says. "He likes a lot of the things that I like, and the idea of us working together is not out of the question for me."

He went on to say that "the subjects he chooses are very interesting to me," and that, aside from "Yellowstone," "other things that he's doing, I think, are really, really good. He likes the same subjects that I do."
Costner ultimately didn't return to film the last episodes of "Yellowstone." (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Airbnb)

Costner ultimately did not return to film the remainder of "Yellowstone" season five. A new spinoff, "Dutton Ranch," continued the Dutton family's story and followed Cole Hauser and Kelly Reilly's characters as they left Montana to start a new life in Texas.
Helen Mirren
Mirren starred in the "Yellowstone" spinoff series "1923." (Karwai Tang/WireImage; Emerson Miller/Paramount+)
Helen Mirren spoke to The Hollywood Reporter in December 2022 at the premiere of "1923."
When speaking with the outlet, she gave fans an inside look at what it's like working with Sheridan, calling him "fabulously hands-off."

"He presents the script, and it’s so extraordinary that you don’t want to change a word. You want to do it exactly as it’s written because it’s written with incredible precision but without being labored," she said. "To be able to be a part of a franchise in a world that is so singular on American television is very exciting. There’s nothing else quite like it."
Brian Geraghty
Geraghty praised Sheraton for his writing and casting ability. (Valerie Terranova/Getty Images for Searchlight Pictures)
"1923" star Brian Geraghty spoke with The Hollywood Reporter at the premiere of the show in December 2022 about his experience working with Sheridan.
Geraghty explained that he "expected someone totally different" prior to meeting Sheridan for the first time, and how his experience as an actor makes him a great showrunner.
'LANDMAN' STAR MICHELLE RANDOLPH STUNS IN BARELY-THERE METALLIC YELLOW BIKINI IN NEW SUMMER PHOTO DUMP

"He told me great stories of his time as an actor, about the process and how he hired some of the younger actors on the show by giving them a break over some really big-name actors," he said. "I love that because we all need that break. I got it 15 or 20 years ago and a few of the actors on the show got that from him."
He explained that his experience as an actor makes him "really empathetic to actor," although he presents as "this tough cowboy."
Geraghty starred in the "Yellowstone" spinoff, "1923." (Rodin Eckenroth/WireImage)

"I think he casts really well, and he does not care what you have done, for the most part. He casts the people who are right for the role," he explained. "When you show up to work, everyone raises the bar. He creates that, and it starts from him, but he also is very welcoming and gives you the tools you need to get there."
Michelle Randolph
Michelle Randolph played Elizabeth Strafford in "1923." (James Minchin III/Paramount+)
Michelle Randolph, who has appeared in both "1923" and "Landman," echoed Geraghty's statement and credited Sheridan for being willing to give unknown actors a break.

When speaking to People in 2025, Randolph praised Sheridan as "one of the few people" in the business who "takes chances on actors" and who "has given us this opportunity, and I just am eternally grateful for him."
"He made my dreams come true. I tell him that every time I see him," Randolph said. "He's like, 'Michelle, stop. I get it.' I'm like, 'Thank you.' But he really did give us something."

In addition to praising his casting methods, Randolph also complimented him as a writer, telling The Hollywood Reporter in December 2022 that he gives his characters "such depth and such unique storylines."
Randolph credits Sheridan for changing her life by taking a chance on her as an actress. (Gilbert Flores/WWD via Getty Images)

"No matter how many different situations are going on at once," she said. "Every character is so uniquely themselves and that’s really hard to do as a writer, especially for the amount of shows that he’s writing for."
Kurt Russell
Russell said "The Madison" is Sheridan's best writing. (Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)
Kurt Russell could not help but praise Sheridan's writing ability while at the premiere of "The Madison" in March.

"I love his writing. I think this is his best writing. I love that this is not 'Yellowstone.' It's not that. It's very, it's very standalone, very different," he told Page Six. "I love the relationships that he digs into here. And I think that this is truly a different wheelhouse for him. It was fun to do."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Ali Larter
Larter, who plays Angela in "Landman," revealed she knew Sheridan prior to being cast on the show but hadn't spoken to him in a decade. (Emerson Miller/Paramount+)
Ali Larter has developed a close friendship with Sheridan through working with him on "Landman."
When speaking with People in April, Larter shared that Sheridan will often text her as he is writing, saying "if he’s laughing at his own writing… I’ll get a text."

"I mean, you know, the first season, I spent a ton of time with Taylor," she said. "He has a very clear vision of what he wants… and he is a visionary because when he is writing the scripts, he knows how he’s going to edit them."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
She went on to say that, as actors, they often "want to advocate for your character," but Sheridan is "brilliant" at creating a world "where that fits into the story that he wants to tell."
Larter credited Sheridan for being an amazing writer. (Emerson Miller/Paramount+)
Larter also praised his writing ability and work ethic when speaking with Taste of Country, calling him "the best working writer."
"He's brilliant at the way he crafts his stories," she said. "I love the characters he creates, because they're dynamic and powerful ... But he also has space to show their vulnerable sides."
When speaking with The Hollywood Reporter in June, Larter shared that she and Sheridan knew one another before "Landman," but that they hadn't spoken in over a decade when she was cast on the show.
Larter called Sheridan "an extraordinarily hard worker." (GC Images)

"I don’t think that you can pin him down," she told the outlet. "I think that he’s not going to come back into the machine that just wants to break him down. And he wants to work. He’s an extraordinarily hard worker. He’s a brilliant talent. He wants to do it his way. And I think that it’s very hard in our industry to do things your own way when you’re part of the machine."

title: Jessica Simpson turns heads in bikini photos from trip to Turks and Caicos
summary: Jessica Simpson shared bikini photos from her Turks and Caicos birthday trip on Instagram, lounging in a black polka dot two-piece in paradise.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Jessica Simpson is giving fans a peek at her birthday trip to the Turks and Caicos Islands.
The 46-year-old singer took to Instagram to share a series of photos from her birthday trip to paradise, including one of her lounging in her bikini.

title: Henry Winkler opens up about the unexpected career he considered before becoming an actor
summary: Henry Winkler almost studied to become a child psychologist before transitioning into a career as an actor and finding fame as Fonzie on "Happy Days."
story: Henry Winkler says he formed a friendship with Adam Sandler after he called to thank him for including him in his 'Chanukah Song.’
Henry Winkler is opening up about what career path he would have chosen had he not gotten into acting.

During a recent interview on the "You Could Make This Beautiful" podcast, the 80-year-old actor shared that he almost decided to become a child psychologist, because he was so dyslexic that "whatever I could do, with the least amount of education" was what he wanted to do.

"I understand children. I’m able to listen, I think, to children. I’m interested in what they have to say and how they are. I marvel at their prowess in the universe," Winkler said. "Yes, I would work with children."
Ultimately, the actor found fame playing Arthur "Fonzie" Fonzarelli on "Happy Days" from 1974 to 1984, a role which earned him three Emmy Award nominations.
Winkler shared he thought about becoming a child psychologist before going into acting. (Olivia Wong/WireImage)
'HAPPY DAYS' STAR HENRY WINKLER FILMED HIS FIRST-EVER NUDE SCENE AT 79
The actor has spoken about his lifelong struggle with dyslexia many times in the past and about how he learned to manage it in his career.

"Destiny is very strange, because I've chosen a profession that is so unbelievably difficult, not only to survive in, but to participate in for me," he told "PBS News Weekend" in November 2023. "When we were doing 'Happy Days' or any table read, which is the whole cast all the producers, the directors, everybody on the crew listening, for the first time to the script. I couldn't read off the page. And it was embarrassing. It was humiliating. I covered it with humor."

To manage the obstacles dyslexia presented in his career, Winkler explained that he would "literally read one word at a time" and ask for the script to be delivered to him ahead of time so that he would "almost memorize it" so that by the time it came to the table read, "I could read it with a flow."

While the actor had struggled with dyslexia his whole life, he didn't receive a diagnosis until he was in he was 31, and his young stepson was diagnosed with it, telling PBS that he was initially angry after getting the diagnosis.
Winkler didn't receive a dyslexia diagnosis until he was in his 30s, when his stepson was diagnosed. (MEGA/GC Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I was because I was humiliated. I was constantly browbeaten. I was punished, grounded for most of my life," he said. "Then the next stage was all right, so I have this thing. Now I have to learn to negotiate it because it doesn't go away. It is the wiring in your brain."

He later learned to reframe the situation and began thinking, "maybe I would not be sitting in this chair" if he hadn't gone through "the challenge to constantly work through that made my tenacity, like steel."
Following his time on "Happy Days," Winkler continued acting, introducing himself to a younger audience in the 1998 movie, "The Waterboy," alongside Adam Sandler.

He then appeared in TV shows such as "Arrested Development," "Parks and Recreation" and "New Girl," before landing a starring role in the hit HBO Max show, "Barry," playing Gene Cousineau, an acting coach who finds himself befriending an assassin.

title: Roger Miller given stark choice after getting caught stealing: ‘You can go to jail or you can go in the Army’
summary: Dean Miller says his father joined the Army as a teen after he was caught stealing from a club. The judge then gave him a choice between jail and the Army.
story: Country music star Lee Greenwood discusses the re-launch of his distillery, Soldier Valley Spirits, ahead of America's 250th birthday on 'America Reports.'
Roger Miller's son is getting candid about why his famous father joined the Army as a teenager.

During a recent interview on the "Drifting Cowboy" podcast, the country music legend's son, Dean Miller, discussed how his father grew up "on a farm with no electricity" and would spend the weekends driving to Amarillo, Texas, to play shows at a nightclub in an effort to break into the music industry.

"He would play at this one club, and he was friends with the guy and my dad, as he describes it, was ignorant and didn't know how to break into show business or how to get out of town or what to do with his life," he said.

Dean explained that his dad later had the idea that "if he stole a bunch of stuff from this club, he'd have all he needed to be in show business," leading him to steal equipment and costumes. According to the singer's website, he stole a guitar because he wanted it "so desperately to write songs," and turned himself in the next day.
The country singer's son recalled how his father ended up in the Army. (Silver Screen Collection/Hulton Archive/Getty Images)

"The police caught him and the guy that he stole from wrote a letter to the judge and said, 'Please be lenient on this kid. He doesn't know any better. He's a good kid.' And all this stuff," Dean said. "And so they told my dad, 'You can go to jail or you can go in the Army. Your choice.' And he chose the Army."
After joining the Army, Roger was deployed to Korea during the Korean War, which he referred to as the "Korea Clash of '52."
Dean recalled his father telling him that while in Korea, "I just spent the whole time hiding under a jeep and crying."

Ultimately, his time in the Army helped him in his music career, with Dean saying that is where "he met people in music" and was able to get "recommendations to people back home and started coming to Nashville after that."
Miller won 11 Grammy Awards in two years, and was nominated for a total of 18. (Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

It was while he was in the Army that he met his longtime friend and writing partner, Bill Anderson. The two would go on to write many hit songs together, including "When Two Worlds Collide," which became a Top 10 hit.
Roger is often regarded as a major figure in country music, credited for broadening the range of the genre by including elements of pop music in his songs.

Between 1965 and 1966, Roger won 11 Grammy Awards, including best contemporary country album for "Dang Me/Chug-A-Lug," and best country song for "Dang Me" and "King of the Road." He received a total of 18 nominations.

He also wrote the score for the Broadway musical "Big River," and the soundtrack for the Disney movie "Robin Hood." He was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1995, three years after his death.

Kacey Musgraves called Roger Miller an icon. (Timothy Norris/Getty Images)

To me, if you look beyond the box, the whole world is waiting — no matter what you call the music, just be true to what you're doing."

"I went to England in 2019, and when I went there, you know, my body just exploded," Love said in an Instagram video.

"When I was a kid — and I think this record is about this — I used to pattern interrupt the adults," she said. "They’d tell me red was blue, and then I’d see blue, but blue was blue.

A California actor and producer is facing 24 felony charges after investigators said he used online casting calls to contact minors as part of an alleged pattern of child sexual abuse spanning decades.
Shane Ryan Gledhill, 46, of Lompoc, was arrested Aug. 3 after Santa Barbara County Sheriff's detectives spent nearly five years investigating accusations of exploitation.
Gledhill, whose work involved projects connected to actors including Shelley Duvall, Tom Arnold, Richard Dreyfuss and Ed Harris, was initially booked on 15 felony charges.
That total has now climbed to 24.
TIMOTHY BUSFIELD INDICTED ON CHILD SEX ABUSE CHARGES IN NEW MEXICO
Shane Ryan Gledhill was arrested Aug. 3. (Santa Barbara Sheriff)

The investigation began in November 2021, when a 17-year-old survivor approached Santa Barbara County Sheriff's investigators about what the alleged victim described as suspicious and inappropriate conduct involving Gledhill when she was 15, according to authorities.
That initial report led to an investigation that eventually identified nine survivors, the sheriff's office said. All were minors at the time of the alleged offenses.
In February 2022, investigators executed a search warrant at his home in Lompoc. Investigators seized thousands of digital files, which underwent an extensive forensic examination.
The sheriff's office said the investigation uncovered a pattern in which Gledhill allegedly used online casting calls and film-making projects to contact aspiring young actors.

Gledhill is being held at the Santa Barbara County jail in California. (Frazer Harrison/Getty Images)

"Individuals who interacted with him under those names may not recognize his legal name. Detectives hope the photograph will assist in identifying additional survivors or witnesses."

The charges against Gledhill include alleged offenses such as child molestation, rape, forcible sexual assault, contacting a minor with the intent to commit a sexual offense, possession of child sexual abuse material and providing harmful matter to a minor.
Gledhill was taken into custody at his Lompoc home on an arrest warrant and booked into the Northern Branch Jail. His bail was set at $2 million.
"Based on evidence developed during the investigation, detectives believe there may be additional survivors who have not yet been identified or come forward," the press release shared.

title: ‘A Man Without Love’ singer Engelbert Humperdinck credits underwater workout for keeping him ‘alive’ at 90
summary: Engelbert Humperdinck reveals the underwater pool workout and martial arts routine he credits with keeping him "alive" and performing at age 90.

At 90, Engelbert Humperdinck has an unusual workout routine he credits with keeping him alive and going strong.
The British singer, known as the "King of Romance," recently appeared on "The Jim Masters Show," where he shared his unconventional exercise regimen.

"I walk out in the pool all the day," he told the host. "I do all my martial art moves in the pool underwater, which makes it even more effective. … And that’s how I stay alive and keep going and keep myself as fit as possible so that the audience can see me in a respectable way.
JOAN COLLINS SHARES HER SIMPLE SECRETS TO AGING GRACEFULLY AT 93
Engelbert Humperdinck performs at Kiri Te Kanawa Theatre June 30, 2026, in Auckland, New Zealand. (Dave Simpson/WireImage)
"That's where I work out there in the pool," he said. "I do all my stuff up there, which is great."
And it appears to be working. The "Release Me" singer is still performing regularly, with concert dates scheduled into 2027 abroad. He's also preparing to release a new album, "Faithfully," Aug. 28.
The album features Humperdinck putting his own spin on songs by Journey, the Cars, Kiss and Aerosmith, with several guest musicians joining him on the record.

While Humperdinck is working to keep his body young, a decades-old song is helping him reach younger audiences. His 1968 track "A Man Without Love" was featured in two episodes of Marvel Studios' "Moon Knight."
Engelbert Humperdinck poses at his home on a Harley-Davidson with a Union flag before traveling to Baku for Eurovision on May 8, 2012, in Leicester, England. (Christopher Furlong/Getty Images)

"Since ‘Man Without Love,’ it’s triggered something off," he said. "And it’s so nice. It’s so nice to know that people are now not worried about an age. They’re worried about the music, and that’s all that counts as far as I’m concerned. But I try to stay as young as possible all the time."

While Humperdinck continues connecting with audiences through the love songs that made him famous, the lyrics have taken on a deeper meaning since his wife, Patricia, died in 2021 after living with Alzheimer's disease and contracting COVID-19. The couple married in 1964 and remained together for 57 years until her death at age 85.

"She’s the backbone. She was the backbone to my whole life, I think, because she started with me when I was nobody. … And so she was instrumental in the early years. And when I really made it in the industry and got a family, I used to have to leave home for about three months at a time. And she raised the children by herself."

"There's no better feeling. There's no better feeling than walking on stage," he said. "I call myself a thespian of song. So, when I'm singing, I act a part. It's not acting really, it's reality coming through. But I give my all, and I read the lyrics a little differently now, especially since I lost my wife. And it comes out more sincere.

Carmen Electra is in the summer 2026 issue of Playboy available now. (Gerome Defrance/Getty Images)

"I still like a guy that's a little bit edgy, but I wouldn't mind being with a dad type," the star told Fox News Digital. "I did actually date a dad. He had a daughter. I fell in love with the daughter. And I kind of thought that was going to be the relationship. Didn't work out, but I could be with someone who has a kid or not."
Carmen Electra plays celebrity bunny dealer at the Playboy Club at The Palms Hotel in Las Vegas Dec. 13, 2008. (Jon Kopaloff/FilmMagic)

The actress and model has walked down the aisle twice before. She wed former NBA star Dennis Rodman in November 1998. Rodman filed for an annulment just nine days later, though the pair reconciled before Electra ultimately filed for divorce in April 1999.
Electra gave marriage another shot with Jane's Addiction guitarist Dave Navarro, saying "I do" in 2003. The couple announced their separation in 2006, and their divorce was finalized in 2007.
CARMEN ELECTRA REVEALS HER SIMPLE RULE FOR KEEPING THE ‘SPARK ALIVE’ IN RELATIONSHIPS
Today, Electra isn't putting any limits on love.

"They don't have to be a dad," she said. "They could be a little bit younger. I don't know. I don't really know who that guy is yet. I work really hard. I make money. I'm not looking for the man with money. That's not my goal.
"If he wants to buy me a few gifts, that's nice. But I can take care of myself. He just has to be a good person. That's very important. And we have to like the same things.

For the summer 2026 issue, Carmen Electra steps in as Playboy advisor and answered pressing questions about love and dating to field readers’ questions about love, confidence and reinvention. (Max Montgomery for Playboy)

"It's also cool when opposites attract," she noted. "Because they say if two people are too similar, one person is unnecessary. So, you don't want it to be too similar, but you do want to like certain things. You want to have some things in common. But you also want to learn from each other."
Electra has long worn her heart on her sleeve and "love" on her skin. The pinup previously told Fox News Digital she has the word tattooed on her wrist.
Carmen Electra has racked up more than 150 covers worldwide. (Max Montgomery for Playboy)

"I've always been about love," Electra said at the time. "I've always come from a place of love. And if we could all do that, what a wonderful place we could be in. If you really mess with me, I don't know how much love you're going to get. But I truly believe in love."
Electra said she has felt plenty of love from her social media followers, who have cheered her on through the years.
Carmen Electra arrives at The Abbey's 35th Anniversary at The Abbey Food & Bar in West Hollywood May 20, 2026. (Steve Granitz/FilmMagic/Getty Images)

"Look, sometimes I'm trying different things on my Instagram page," she said. "Not everyone's going to love those things, and you might not get as many likes. But you turn around and, boom, my fans are there."

Carmen Electra joined "Baywatch" for its eighth season. (Gerome Defrance/Getty Images)

After making a splash in Hollywood, Electra has discovered what makes her feel most confident, and it has nothing to do with looking glamorous or having a beau. For her, it's all about being booked and busy.

"I feel the most confident when I'm working, and I've been working a lot," she said. "When I'm working, I'm really happy. It's weird; you would think that by now I'd be over it. But I'm just not. I love it. And the more I work, the more confident I feel. When I'm in love, I feel confident. But I don't have someone in my life right now. But I'm still confident because I'm working."
Carmen Electra attends the "Scary Movie" global premiere at Paramount Pictures Studios June 3, 2026, in Los Angeles. (Getty Images for Paramount Pictures)
After returning to Playboy, Electra has a message for women who think getting older means fading into the background: Don't buy it.

Carmen Electra is in the new issue of Playboy alongside cover girl Cara Delevingne. (Max Montgomery for Playboy)

"Don't let anyone tell you you're too old," she said. "That's a myth. You are living your own life. You're not living your life for other people. And, honestly, if you're manifesting that, that's what it's going to be for you.

"You have to change your thought process. You have to start telling yourself every morning, 'I'm beautiful. I'm good enough. I look great. I'm pretty.' Whatever it is that you want to be, you can be that.
Carmen Electra arrives at the world premiere of "Infinite Icon: A Visual Memoir" at AMC The Grove 14 in Los Angeles Jan. 20, 2026. (Steve Granitz/FilmMagic)

"At one time in my life, I was reading a lot of books about Buddhism," she reflected. "I remember one book talked about your inner child and never losing your inner child. And I've always been a bit childish.

"So, I always thought, 'I'm not going to lose it.' I never want to lose that, and I'm not going to. And I think the people who are older than me, who are still in this business and who I think are beautiful, have a youthful spirit. And people will love you for being who you really, truly are."

title: Carly Simon seemingly takes aim at ex James Taylor on new album as she sings, 'Maybe I never loved you'
summary: Carly Simon's new album, "Comes in Waves," features a track that appears aimed at ex-husband James Taylor, questioning whether their love ever existed.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Carly Simon appears to take aim at ex-husband James Taylor with a five-word bombshell: "Maybe I never loved you."
The Grammy-winning singer seems to turn the wreckage of their decade-long marriage into a song on her new album, "Comes in Waves."
"Maybe I never loved you / But anyway, I thought I did," Simon sings on the album’s second track. "I married you, we had a kid / That counts for something."
‘YOU’RE SO VAIN’ SINGER CARLY SIMON SAYS PARKINSON’S AND CANCER DIAGNOSES KEPT HER FROM PUBLIC EYE
James Taylor and Carly Simon circa 1979 in New York City. (Robin Platzer/Images/Getty Images)
She immediately undercuts her own certainty, wondering whether she did love her former husband — and whether he ever truly loved her.
"Maybe I never loved you / Yes, and maybe I did," she sings. "And maybe you never loved me / Although God knows, you said you did."
Taylor is never identified by name.
Simon was married to the "Fire and Rain" singer from 1972 to 1983. Their relationship was rocky and remained in the public eye for decades.
"You came for me those times I hid / I’m so glad you did that," she sings. "And maybe it’s wrong to wonder how everything kind became forbidden."
Carly Simon returns after an 18-year hiatus with song lyrics seemingly directed at her ex, James Taylor. (Richard E. Aaron/Redferns)
The song eventually concludes with what sounds like a final attempt at closure.
"And maybe it’s best to bury whatever it was we had our fill of," she sings. "Maybe I never loved you / Maybe I always will."
Fox News Digital has reached out to both Simon and Taylor for comment.
In a 2015 interview with People, Simon said she and Taylor had not spoken in more than a decade.
"I still want to heal him. I still want to make him all right," she said. "And I love him so much."
Simon said Taylor's treatment of her had been deeply painful, but writing her memoir helped her understand something about herself and about unrequited love.
IN MEMOIR, CARLY SIMON REVEALS SHE USED 'SPANISH WITCH DOCTOR' TO HELP SAVE HER MARRIAGE
Carly Simon sings, "Maybe I never loved you / Maybe I always will" in her new song, "Maybe I Never Loved You" from her latest album. (Bettmann)

"My incredible loyalty to him, in spite of the fact that he has treated me without any regard, has been so painful to me for so long," she told the outlet. "But, through the course of writing the book, I really started to understand that I could love and not be loved. And that was the big realization for me, that it doesn’t have to be a two-way street."
The deeply personal album arrives as Simon has also been navigating significant health challenges away from the spotlight.
The "You’re So Vain" singer has Parkinson’s disease and recently had surgery for basal cell carcinoma, a form of skin cancer.
Simon explained to People why she had largely stayed out of the public eye.
Carly Simon appears to address her marriage and divorce from James Taylor on her new album, "Comes in Waves." (Clint Spaulding/WWD/Penske Media via Getty Images)
"It has taken me some time to understand the diagnosis, to adjust to it, and to decide how much I wanted to say about it publicly," the 83-year-old told the outlet in a statement published July 27.

"Parkinson's is different for everyone, and it can be unpredictable," she continued. "Some days I'm so tired I can't get the day moving at all. On others, it gives me a little more room to move, think, work and feel like myself."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Her comments offer a rare glimpse into what the legendary singer has been experiencing privately while continuing to create music.
Her latest project, "Comes in Waves," marks the end of an 18-year hiatus from releasing original music, and she's looking squarely at the past while confronting the realities of the present.
Simon and Taylor were one of music's ultimate power couples of the 1970s.
Their romance moved fast. Simon said she went to Taylor's dressing room at New York's Carnegie Hall in 1971 after seeing him perform.
On July 27, 2026, Carly Simon told People magazine in a statement she has Parkinson’s disease. (Jack Mitchell/Getty Images)

"I have a wonderful history with Carnegie Hall," she said previously in a Harper’s Bazaar interview. "I met James there that same year when I went to his dressing room to say hello, and he invited himself to my home for a late-night lunch that expanded into a life together."
By the following year, they were married.
Their wedding took place Nov. 3, 1972, in a small ceremony at Simon's New York home.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
But the marriage didn't last.
The couple separated in 1981, and their divorce was finalized in 1983. They share two children, Sally Taylor and Ben Taylor.
Behind the scenes, their marriage was unraveling as Taylor struggled with drug addiction. Both Simon and Taylor have acknowledged infidelity during their marriage.
Simon later described their relationship in her 2015 memoir, "Boys in the Trees," as "far from the idyllic one that the general public reads about."
Simon recently underwent surgery for basal cell carcinoma, a form of skin cancer. (Richard E. Aaron/Redferns)
She had an even harsher description of their relationship.
"Our love became bipolar, switching from love to hate, lust to loathing, and back again, sometimes within a day," Simon wrote.
Taylor has also acknowledged how deeply his addiction damaged his relationships.
"You could fall in love, but if one of the people is addicted, it’s not going to work," he told Parade. "The whole person is simply not available."

title: Meghan Markle, Prince Harry's box-office flop shows 'infamy' doesn't equal success: expert
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's Girl Scouts documentary opened in 446 theaters, but royal experts question whether Sussex star power sells tickets.
story: Catherine Mayer, author of "Divide & Rule," explains why Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's departure from royal life dealt a lasting blow to the monarchy and its connection with younger audiences.

Though Prince Harry and Meghan Markle may still dominate headlines, their latest Hollywood venture is raising questions about whether the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's names can convert all that attention into paying customers.

Following the recent release of "Cookie Queens," a documentary executive produced by the couple through Archewell Productions that follows four Girl Scouts navigating the highly competitive world of cookie sales while examining ambition, leadership and adolescence, the movie's opening weekend failed to produce strong box-office numbers.

"Cookie Queens" earned approximately $354,000 from 446 theaters, according to reported box-office figures. The documentary was beaten by "CatVideoFest 2026," a compilation of viral internet cat videos that earned approximately $569,000 despite playing on just 255 screens.
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S HOLLYWOOD DREAMS HIT WALL AS EXPERT WARNS OF ‘TOXIC BRAND’ STIGMA
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle executive produced a new documentary, "Cookie Queens," through Archewell Productions.  (The David Foster Foundation via Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell for comment.
The result has royal experts questioning whether Harry and Meghan's ability to dominate the news cycle still carries the same weight it once did.

"Harry and Meghan remain extraordinarily effective at generating headlines, but headlines and paying customers are two very different things," royal commentator Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube's "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital.
"There was a period when simply attaching their names to something guaranteed enormous curiosity. I’m not convinced that’s true anymore."
MARTHA STEWART QUESTIONS MEGHAN MARKLE’S HOMEMAKING CREDENTIALS WITH BLUNT CAREER ASSESSMENT

"And there’s no getting around the optics of finishing five places behind a 70-minute compilation of internet cat videos. Hollywood can forgive a lot, but being beaten by ‘CatVideoFest’ is the sort of indignity that writes its own punchline."

Alysa Nahmias and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, attend a special screening of Roadside Attractions' "Cookie Queens" at AMC The Grove 14 in Los Angeles on July 28, 2026. (Roadside Attractions via Getty Images)
The Duchess of Sussex personally promoted the documentary ahead of its theatrical debut, discussing the movie and her own childhood experience as a Girl Scout.
Schofield said that involvement makes the opening numbers particularly noteworthy.

"Meghan certainly has enormous name recognition, but I think, at this stage, it’s fair to ask how much of that is fame and how much is infamy," she said. "There’s a significant difference commercially.

"People may click on a Meghan Markle headline because they’re fascinated by her or irritated by her. That doesn’t mean they’re going to buy a movie ticket because her name is attached to the project. ‘Cookie Queens’ gives us another interesting data point on that distinction."
MEGHAN MARKLE'S SHOW EMMY NOMINATION 'SOMEWHAT BAFFLING' DUE TO LACKLUSTER RATINGS: EXPERT

British royals expert Hilary Fordwich shared the same sentiment in that the performance raises questions about the couple's ability to attract audiences when their projects are not centered on the royal family.

"Harry and Meghan remain extraordinarily effective at generating headlines, but headlines and paying customers are two very different things," royal commentator Kinsey Schofield told Fox News Digital. (Chris Jackson/Pool/Getty Images)

"The extremely underwhelming box office is a clear indication that, yet again, unless they are bashing the royals and sharing inside stories, secrets and betraying the privacy of the family, there isn’t much they have that is at all in demand nor popular," Fordwich told Fox News Digital.
"Meghan certainly doesn’t have the commercial pull she has so desired."
Fordwich argued the couple now face increased pressure to demonstrate they can produce a genuine mainstream hit.
OPRAH WINFREY SPARKS FRESH BACKLASH AFTER SHE REVISITS PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE BOMBSHELL INTERVIEW
That question has followed the Sussexes throughout their post-royal entertainment career.

After stepping back from royal duties in 2020 and relocating to California, Harry and Meghan signed major deals in Hollywood. Their Netflix docuseries, "Harry & Meghan," released in 2022, generated enormous attention by focusing heavily on the couple's departure from royal life and their relationship with the monarchy.
The couple stepped back from royal duties in 2020.  (Matt Dunham/WPA Pool/Getty Images)
Harry's 2023 memoir, "Spare," similarly produced worldwide headlines with its claims about life inside the royal family.
Royal expert Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital those projects remain the couple's most significant attention grabbers.

"We all know their huge hits were the three infamous betrayals of the royal family, on Oprah, the Netflix series ‘Harry & Meghan’ and Harry’s memoir ‘Spare,’" Fitzwilliams said. "What is undoubted is the publicity that accompanies everything they do."
WATCH: PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE'S EXIT HURT THE MONARCHY: AUTHOR
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"The world knows who they are but isn't curious enough to tune in and watch Meghan's ghastly series 'With Love, Meghan,' their series on the Invictus Games, 'Polo' or, it seems, 'Cookie Queens.' Reports vary on the exact level of success or failure of Meghan's brand As Ever, but the jam, flower sprinkles and scented candles have become a bit of a joke.
"So, it’s all about buzz and nothing else, save their link with real royalty."
Since relocating to California, both Harry and Meghan have been involved in multiple Hollywood projects.  (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

Still, for Schofield, the numbers connected to "Cookie Queens" add to a broader question involving Archewell as Harry and Meghan move further away from the royal family drama and focus more on their American ventures.
"Harry and Meghan are a fascinating case study in the difference between attention and commercial influence," Schofield said.
PRINCE HARRY LONGS FOR HIS OLD ROYAL LIFE AS AMERICA ISN'T WHAT HE EXPECTED, EXPERTS SAY

"Infamy can be extremely valuable to newspapers, television shows and social media platforms because people will click, argue and engage. Monetizing that attention yourself is a completely different challenge.
"People want to consume content about Harry and Meghan," she added, "but are they equally interested in consuming content from Harry and Meghan?"
A royal expert told Fox News Digital the curiosity surrounding them was "enormous" when they first moved to California.  (Chris Jackson)
Schofield said Hollywood's expectations have changed considerably since the couple first arrived in California.

"When Harry and Meghan first arrived in California, they were the story," she said. "Hollywood was essentially buying access to two people who had just walked away from the royal family, and the curiosity surrounding them was enormous.
"Six years later, the novelty has diminished. The questions are much more conventional now: What can you produce? What can you sell? Can you build an audience around something that isn’t royal drama?
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
"They’ve had the deals, resources and access," she continued. "At this stage, tangible results matter."
Schofield believes the couple's future standing in Hollywood may depend less on announcements and more on execution.
The couple share two children together.  (Angela Weiss)

"Hollywood is full of projects that die in development, so, individually, none of those are necessarily remarkable," she said. "But when you establish a pattern of big announcements without finished products, you risk damaging your credibility.
"You cannot build a serious production reputation on press releases and announcements," Schofield added.
And that, she said, is why even a relatively small documentary such as "Cookie Queens" matters.
"When a project does reach audiences, its performance becomes part of the résumé," Schofield said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Being beaten at the box office by ‘CatVideoFest’ is funny, but against this larger backdrop, it makes the need for a genuine success that much more urgent."

Christina Dugan Ramirez is an entertainment journalist with more than 15 years of experience, including a decade at PEOPLE writing high-profile cover stories, covering Hollywood's biggest events, and interviewing many of the industry's most influential stars before joining Fox News Digital in 2024.

title: Kelly Osbourne blasts Dee Snider as 'spectacularly classless' for claiming Ozzy didn’t write his own songs
summary: Kelly Osbourne called Dee Snider's claims about her father's songwriting "spectacularly classless," igniting a fierce debate over Ozzy Osbourne's legacy.
story: Piers Morgan remembers Ozzy Osbourne after the heavy metal legend was laid to rest in his hometown of Birmingham, England.
Kelly Osbourne and Twisted Sister frontman Dee Snider are going head-to-head after the retired musician claimed Ozzy Osbourne "always" had other people write his songs for him.

Earlier this week, Snider wrote on X, "Ozzy always had bass players write his lyrics." He went on to claim that bassist Bob Daisley and Motörhead frontman Lemmy Kilmister were frequent writers of Ozzy's music, and that Geezer Butler "wrote ALL of @BlackSabbath lyrics."

According to Daisley's website, he claimed to have written the majority of the songs for Ozzy's first five solo albums. Daisley is credited as a songwriter on "Blizzard of Ozz" and "No Rest for the Wicked." During Ozzy's time with Black Sabbath, Butler was widely credited as the main lyricist for the band.
Snider's comments prompted a sharp response from Ozzy's daughter via her Instagram Stories Friday.
KELLY OSBOURNE DEMANDS CHILD SUPPORT AND HER DOGS BACK IN FIERY RANT AMID REPORTED BREAKUP
Kelly Osbourne called out Dee Snider after he claimed Ozzy Osbourne did not always write his own music. (Getty Images)
Kelly shared two text-heavy posts, including one directly addressing Snider.

"My father’s legacy as a musician, songwriter, singer and bandleader speaks for itself. His friends, those who worked with him, those who love him, and millions of fans around the world that still continue to buy his records know exactly what he meant what he contributed and what he leaves behind. His legacy will live on eternally," Kelly wrote on the first image.
Kelly Osbourne addressed Dee Snider's comments on her Instagram Stories. (Kelly Osbourne/Instagram)
KELLY OSBOURNE WELCOMES FIRST BABY WITH SID WILSON, SHARON OSBOURNE PRAISES DAUGHTER: 'SO PROUD'
In her next Instagram story, Kelly called Snider’s criticism "spectacularly classless" and argued that he had little basis to speak authoritatively about her father's career and legacy.
"And if Snider wants to invite comparisons between their careers, that comparison is devastating enough on its own," she wrote.
Kelly Osbourne called out Dee Snider directly on her Instagram story. (Kelly Osbourne/Instagram)

Kelly then compared Snider and Ozzy's careers, writing, "Snider had a brief period of mainstream success more than 40 years ago. My father's career spanned nearly six decades — from helping define heavy metal with Black Sabbath to building an extraordinary solo career. His music will continue influencing generations long after all of us are gone."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Kelly suggested that Snider’s criticism was an attempt to put himself back into the conversation, while her father’s "name, catalogue and influence" remain globally relevant. She argued that Ozzy’s accomplishments stand on their own, writing, "My father doesn’t need Dee Snider’s approval to establish his place in music history."
Kelly Osbourne fiercely protected her late father, Ozzy Osbourne's, legacy. (Kevin Mazur)

She concluded, "trying to make my father smaller won’t make Dee Snider bigger," arguing that attacking Ozzy’s legacy only draws greater attention to the difference between the two musicians’ careers and lasting cultural impact.
Early Friday morning, Snider returned to X to make it clear that he has "nothing but love for Ozzy."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
"He was always lovely to me. @BlackSabbath changed my life! As a songwriter I can be a little touchy about credit and royalties," Snider wrote.
Dee Snider clarified that he has "nothing but love" for Ozzy Osbourne. (Scott Dudelson/Getty Images)
Representatives for Kelly did not respond to Fox News Digital. Snider's representative said the rocker had no further comment.

Ozzy died on July 22, 2025, at 76, just weeks after performing his final concert with Black Sabbath. His death certificate later listed cardiac arrest and coronary artery disease among the causes of his death, with Parkinson’s disease noted as a contributing condition.

summary: Halle Berry marked her 60th birthday with a bold photo slideshow on Instagram, including a romantic shot with fiancé Van Hunt and selfies of her in a robe.
story: ‘The Five’ co-hosts analyze Halle Berry accusing Gov. Gavin Newsom of 'devaluing' women 'in midlife.'

EMILY RATAJKOWSKI'S SHREDDED RED BIRTHDAY DRESS LEAVES LITTLE TO THE IMAGINATION AT NYC CELEBRATION
Berry posted a series of photos on Instagram to celebrate her 60th birthday. (Halle Berry Instagram)
