title: Alaska runner hospitalized after using bear spray to fight off brown bear on Alaska trail
summary: A runner on Anchorage's Wolverine Bowl trail used bear spray to fend off a brown bear and was hospitalized, marking the second attack in the area in weeks.
story: A woman is recovering after a sudden brown bear encounter in Anchorage on July 18, led officers to deploy a drone while firefighters evacuated her down a hillside. (Anchorage Police)
A runner was hospitalized in Alaska after fending off a bear attack in Anchorage this week.
The woman, who was running by herself at Prospect Heights’ Wolverine Bowl trail, was able to get away from the brown bear by using her bear spray, according to the Alaska Department of Fish and Game.
She was taken to a local hospital for treatment.
BEAR ATTACK IN YELLOWSTONE NATIONAL PARK LEAVES 2 HIKERS INJURED
A woman was hospitalized in Alaska after fending off a bear attack this week. (LightRocket via Getty Images, File)
Biologists went to the site of the attack and collected samples but no bears were seen.
The department said anyone who sees a bear or another wild animal acting aggressively or unusually should report it.
Warning signs have been posted at the Prospect Heights trailhead, the departmet said, adding that hikers should stay off closed trails.

"Thick, dense summer foliage can block sightlines, making surprise encounters more likely," the department said. "Choose hiking routes with good visibility and away from known attractants, like salmon-bearing streams."

When hiking in bear country, people should carry a deterrent such as bear spray or a firearm, stay in groups, make noise to avoid surprising a bear, stay alert for signs of bears, don’t approach bears and keep pets on a leash.
WOMAN ATTACKED BY BROWN BEAR WHILE HIKING WITH FRIEND AND 3 DOGS NEAR ALASKA STATE PARK
A view of the downtown skyline in Anchorage, Alaska. (Getty Images)

"If you surprise a bear, especially one with cubs or on a food cache, it may react in a threatened or defensive manner," the department said. "The bear may be agitated and may huff, stomp, make a popping sound with its teeth, salivate or lay its ears back against its head and charge."
They urged staying calm, standing your ground, readying deterrent, staying in a group and talking calmly. Never run.

"If the bear is stationary, move away slowly while keeping your eyes on the bear," the department said. "If the bear starts to move toward you or charges, stop and stand your ground. Let the bear know you are not a threat. Behaving calmly, moving slowly, and speaking in a low calm voice will help de-escalate the situation. If the bear continues to approach, use your deterrent when the bear is within range."
WOMAN STALKED BY CHARGING BEAR ON MORNING DOG WALK CAPTURES TERRIFYING ENCOUNTER ON CAMERA
The attack comes less than a month after another woman was mauled by a bear in Anchorage.
The attack comes less than a month after another woman was mauled by a bear in Anchorage. (LightRocket via Getty Images, File)
The July victim was walking with a friend and her three dogs in the Bear Valley residential neighborhood, adjacent to Chugach State Park in south Anchorage, when the bear approached.

Officials said the hikers were on an unofficial, user-made trail that climbs a steep hillside in a zigzag pattern. The area was heavily overgrown with dense vegetation, which created poor visibility and increased the risk of surprising wildlife, the department said.

"The bear came out of the dense alders, made brief contact with one of the hikers, and left the scene," the department added.
The woman suffered non-life-threatening injuries and was expected to recover.

title: Nevada man funneled 140 guns to violent Mexican drug cartels, including powerful 'military-style' rifles: DOJ
summary: Luis Alberto Osorio admitted to buying 140 firearms, including military-style rifles for violent Mexican drug-trafficking organizations, in a straw purchase scheme.
story: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche has announced law enforcement actions against the Jalisco New Generation Cartel for importing fentanyl into the U.S., operating a timeshare fraud scheme and more.

A Nevada man pleaded guilty on Friday to purchasing high-powered firearms and ammunition to sell to drug-trafficking organizations in Mexico, money laundering and employing people illegally in the U.S., Department of Justice officials said.

Luis Alberto Osorio allegedly conspired with co-defendants between April 2020 and last September to buy 140 firearms, magazines, and ammunition for people affiliated with violent Mexican drug-trafficking cartels, which would be sold south of the border for a profit, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Nevada.

The guns included large caliber and long-range firearms such as the Ohio Ordnance Works M2-SLR .50 BMG, the Barrett M82A1 and M107A1 .50 BMG antimaterial rifles, the FN Herstal M249S 5.56x45mm and the FH Herstal SCAR 17S 7.62x51mm rifles, according to court documents.
Osorio also admitted to employing people in the U.S. illegally at a mining company in Nevada.
BORDER AGENTS UNCOVER RPG LAUNCHER, CACHE OF RIFLES HIDDEN IN VEHICLE HEADING TO MEXICO

According to court documents, Osorio conspired with co-defendants between April 2020 and last September to buy 140 firearms, magazines and ammunition for people allegedly affiliated with violent Mexican drug-trafficking cartels. (Getty Images, File)

Osorio, of Elko, pleaded guilty to one count of straw purchasing of firearms; one count of trafficking in firearms; one count of harboring certain aliens; and one count of conspiracy to launder money.
He faces a maximum of 70 years in prison.

"Firearms trafficking networks feed the violent cartels that terrorize border communities and pump illicit drugs into our neighborhoods," First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada said in a statement. "By cutting off this supply chain and holding this defendant accountable, we are directly disrupting the operational capabilities of these dangerous criminal organizations."
FBI CHARGES 35 IN WEST VIRGINIA DRUG AND FIREARMS OPERATION, LAUNCHES NATIONWIDE SUMMER CRIME INITIATIVE
Osario’s sentencing is scheduled for February.

"Trafficking military-style firearms and ammunition to drug trafficking organizations in Mexico fuels violence, strengthens criminal networks and threatens communities on both sides of the border," said Jonathan Sherwin, deputy special agent in charge of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Las Vegas. "This guilty plea is the result of relentless work by HSI and the Homeland Security Task Force and our federal, state and local partners to disrupt the flow of weapons, money and criminal support that allows these organizations to operate."
A burned truck is seen as members of the Civil Guard of Michoacan patrol a highway after a wave of cartel violence in Aguililla, Mexico. (AFP via Getty Images, File)
The case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force initiative, which was created by an executive order President Donald Trump signed on his first day in office last year.

"In the world of organized crime and drug trafficking, guns and drugs go hand-in-hand," David S. Olesky, special agent in charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration Los Angeles Field Division, which covers Nevada, said in a statement.

"As a member of the Homeland Security Task Force, DEA and our partners will bring to bear all resources and draw on the full scope of our agencies’ expertise to hold accountable those individuals and organizations which pose a public health and safety threat to our communities through the trafficking of drugs and firearms."

title: Ex-detective who served fraction of 102-year sentence faces new charges after cold case review
summary: Former Los Angeles vice detective Michael Douglas Brambles, paroled in 2020 under California's elderly inmates law, faces new kidnapping charges.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on Foxnews.com.

A former Los Angeles vice detective who was sentenced to 102 years in prison three decades ago for multiple rapes but paroled in 2020 because of a California law was arrested again this week, authorities said.

Michael Douglas Brambles, 77, is charged with kidnapping to commit robbery while personally using a firearm in connection with an alleged robbery and sexual assault, according to the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office.

He also faces several aggravating circumstances, "including that the crime involved great violence, the victim was particularly vulnerable, the manner in which the crime was carried out indicated planning, sophistication or professionalism, and that Brambles engaged in violent conduct indicating a serious danger to society," the district attorney’s office said.
CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM

Michael Douglas Brambles, 77, is charged with kidnapping to commit robbery while personally using a firearm in connection with an alleged robbery and sexual assault, according to the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office. (Ventura County District Attorney's Office; Lou Benoist/ AFP via Getty Images)

Brambles allegedly entered Arabella’s Boutique in Thousand Oaks, California, when a woman identified as SW was closing, pointed a handgun at her, and forced her into the backroom where he tied her hands behind her back and sexually assaulted her.
He is also accused of stealing from the business before he left.
The sexual assault allegations cannot be charged because the statute of limitations has passed.
Shortly after the crime, Brambles was identified as a suspect, but he was already being prosecuted for a string of robberies and sexual assaults.
He was convicted on 26 counts, including 18 armed robberies and multiple sexual assaults.
After being sentenced to 102 years, SW’s case was dismissed, which she agreed with, believing he would spend the rest of his life in prison.
But he was able to apply for parole in 2020 under a California law that allows elderly inmates to apply.
NEWSOM-BACKED LAW LETS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHILD RAPIST SEEK EARLY RELEASE AGAIN AS DA URGES 'STOP THE MADNESS'
Victim SW speaks at the Ventura County District Attorney's Office press conference this week. (Ventura County District Attorney's Office)
At his parole hearing, Brambles denied sexually assaulting any women besides the cases he had already been convicted for in Los Angeles County.
While examining SW’s cold case as part of the federal Sexual Assault Kit Initiative, Ventura County District Attorney’s Office investigators realized he had been paroled.
Brambles was arrested on Wednesday and is being held in Ventura County on $2 million bail.

"A few months ago, when investigators from the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office contacted me, I was shocked to hear not only that this man was walking free, but that he had been out of prison for six years," SW said at a press conference this week. "The justice that I and his other victims deserved was denied when he was only required to serve a fraction of the sentence he earned. I am thankful to have this opportunity now to seek justice for myself and for his other victims."
HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER
The Ventura County District Attorney's office in California. (Ventura County District Attorny's Office/Facebook)
Brambles faces a maximum sentence of 12 years to life if convicted.

"Without her courage, bravery and resolve to once again face the person who allegedly attacked her, we would not be here today," District Attorney Erik Nasarenko said of SW at the press conference. "Despite the passage of time and the long road ahead, SW is committed to seeing Michael Brambles held responsible for these violent accusations from 32 years ago, and so are we."

title: Florida middle school teacher admits to years of 'inappropriate' conversations with former student: deputies
summary: Christian Schneider, a Memorial Middle School teacher, allegedly sent inappropriate messages to a former teenage student since 2023, authorities say.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Florida middle school teacher was arrested after investigators said he exchanged inappropriate messages with a former teenage student and acknowledged communicating inappropriately with the student since 2023.
Christian Schneider, 31, a teacher at Memorial Middle School, was arrested Friday on charges of three felonies following an investigation by the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office.

Detectives opened a criminal investigation into Schneider on July 28, and learned he had been sending inappropriate messages to a former teenage student at Franklin Middle School, according to the sheriff's office.
KENTUCKY MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER ACCUSED OF CROSSING THE LINE WITH STUDENT, ARRESTED UNDER NEW ANTI-GROOMING LAW

Christian Schneider, 31, a teacher at Memorial Middle School, was arrested on Aug. 14, 2026, on three felony charges, according to the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office. (Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office)
Schneider told deputies he had engaged in inappropriate communication with the student since 2023, authorities said.
Authorities have not disclosed the student's exact age, how investigators learned about the alleged communications or further details about the messages.
Schneider faces two counts of solicitation or possession of child sexual abuse material, both second-degree felonies, according to Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office booking records.
He also faces one count of unlawful use of a two-way communications device, a third-degree felony.
HIGH SCHOOL COUNSELOR PLEADS GUILTY TO MULTIPLE SEX CRIMES INVOLVING TEEN SHE WAS MEANT TO HELP
The Hillsborough County Sheriff's office said the investigation remains active. (Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office)
The booking records list July 3 as the offense date for each of the three charges.
Schneider was arrested shortly after noon Friday and booked into custody that afternoon, according to jail records.
Each charge carried a $2,500 surety bond, for a combined $7,500. Schneider was released on surety bond at 2:38 a.m. local time Saturday, jail records show.

"Teachers hold a position of trust that comes with enormous responsibility," said Sheriff Chad Chronister. "When that trust is exploited, it's not just a crime, it's a violation of everything our schools are supposed to stand for. Detectives will continue investigating these cases aggressively, and anyone who abuses their position with a child will be held accountable."
The sheriff's office identified Schneider as a teacher at Memorial Middle School and the teenager as his former student at Franklin Middle School.
Memorial Middle School in Tampa, Florida, where Christian Schneider worked as a teacher at the time of his arrest, according to the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office. (Google Maps)
The agency did not provide additional details about Schneider's connection to Franklin Middle School or when he taught the student.

The sheriff's office said the investigation remains active and that additional information will be released as it becomes available.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Hillsborough County school district for information about Schneider's employment status and for comment on his arrest.

title: Florida cold case suspect allegedly confesses to 1987 murder and reveals secret crime scene details
summary: A Florida man allegedly called police to confess to a 1987 Jacksonville murder, describing crime scene details that had never been publicly released.
story: The Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office announced the arrest of 70-year-old Gary Edward Glowacz in the 1987 killing of Melissa Ellison. (Jacksonville Sheriff's Office via Facebook)

A Florida man charged in the 1987 killing of a 20-year-old mother allegedly confessed after contacting authorities himself, and investigators say he described details of the crime that had never been publicly released.

Gary Edward Glowacz, 70, was charged with second-degree murder and armed burglary with assault or battery in the death of Melissa Ellison, who was found dead inside her Jacksonville home Dec. 28, 1987, according to court records obtained by Fox News Digital.
Ellison was found lying on her bed after her roommates first discovered her 13-month-old child crying on a couch in the living room, according to Glowacz’s arrest report.
TIPSTER CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER POLICE SAY ANONYMOUS CALL HELPED SOLVE 30-YEAR DISAPPEARANCE

Investigators said Ellison had suffered blunt-force trauma to the head and neck. Blood was found on the sheets, her head had been positioned below a pillow and a nightgown had been pulled over her waistline, according to the arrest report.
Detectives also found soot or ash on the bed that they said was consistent with a wooden log having been used to strike her.
Melissa Ellison's body was found by authorities in her bed with injuries consistent with blunt force trauma, according to police. (Jacksonville County Sheriff's Office)
The case remained unsolved for decades.

On July 8, 2026, Glowacz called authorities in Clay County and said he wanted to "set things straight" about Ellison’s death, according to an arrest report. Police said he told a deputy he had committed a burglary at the home and had struck Ellison with a log.
KILLER ADMITS TO DECADES-OLD COLD CASE SLAYING AFTER INVESTIGATORS LEAN ON NEW FORENSIC EVIDENCE: OFFICIALS
During a subsequent interview with Jacksonville cold case detectives, Glowacz allegedly said he had been using drugs at the time and entered the home looking for money or property he could sell.

Glowacz told detectives he found Ellison and her baby in a bedroom, left the room, picked up a wooden log inside the house and returned, according to the report. He allegedly said he struck Ellison once in the head, then carried the child into the living room and placed the baby on a couch.
Melissa Ellison, 20, was found dead in her Jacksonville, Fla., home in December 1987. Authorities announced an arrest in the cold case nearly four decades later. (Jacksonville Sheriff's Office)
Police said Glowacz then returned to the bedroom to look for money.
He allegedly told detectives he pulled Ellison’s body by the legs and lifted a corner of the mattress while searching underneath it.

Investigators said those details closely matched evidence documented inside the home in 1987.
The arrest report says Glowacz accurately described the layout of the house and where the log had been located.
Detectives wrote that those details had not previously been released publicly and were not contained in the article Glowacz said he read before contacting authorities.

title: Police announce arrest after 5 wounded in Virginia State University shooting: report
summary: Multiple victims were transported to area hospitals Saturday morning after a shooting near the Quad Annexes at Virginia State University, campus police says.
story: The ‘Fox & Friends Weekend’ panel gives the latest on a reported shooting at Virginia State University.
At least five people were shot at Virginia State University (VSU) Saturday morning, and one remains in critical condition, according to university officials and the VSU Police Department.
Police arrested 19-year-old Camron Harris of Henrico, Virginia, on Saturday after finding him hiding in a dormitory closet on campus in connection with the shooting, The Associated Press reported.
Harris is not a VSU student, Chesterfield County Police said.

Police obtained eight felony warrants in connection with the case, including for malicious wounding and use of a firearm in the commission of a felony, according to the AP. It was not immediately clear whether Harris had an attorney who could speak on his behalf.

"Officers responded to the 3300 block of Boisseau Street at approximately 1:28 a.m. and discovered five individuals suffering from gunshot wounds outside VSU residence halls," a university official told Fox News Digital.
STUDENT PERPETRATES DEADLY SHOOTING AT THAILAND HIGH SCHOOL, AUTHORITIES SAY
There has been a massive police presence on the Virginia State University campus after an early morning shooting. (WRLH-WWBT)
"All five were transported to area hospitals. One individual is currently in critical condition. The remaining four sustained non-life-threatening injuries."
The university said earlier on X that the shooting involved "multiple suspects." No arrests have been announced.
Police had not provided additional information Saturday evening about whether authorities were still searching for other suspects.
VSU, a state-supported HBCU, is located in Ettrick, Virginia, about 25 miles south of Richmond.
HOUSTON POLICE SHOOT GUNMAN WHO INDISCRIMINATELY FIRED ON VEHICLES, INJURING A MOTHER AND DAUGHTER
A street on Virginia State University's campus Saturday, after at least five people were shot early in the morning. (WRLH-WWBT)

One of the victims was confirmed to be a VSU student. The student was among those who sustained non-life-threatening injuries and has been released from a hospital, the university said in a statement.
Police said the five people who were shot range in age from 17 to 23. Four are not VSU students. The VSU student is 20 years old. The victims' names have not been released.
Authorities have not disclosed a possible motive.
VSU police earlier revealed that the shooting occurred near the school's Quad Annexes student housing complex.
SEVERAL PEOPLE DEAD, INCLUDING SUSPECT, IN RURAL MICHIGAN MULTI-SCENE SHOOTING: POLICE
According to the university, law enforcement "does not believe there is an immediate threat to the VSU campus community."

"We recognize the concern this incident has caused among our students, parents, alumni, friends and the broader VSU community," the university said in a statement Saturday afternoon. "VSU police will maintain an increased presence on campus as the investigation continues.
"Students should monitor their VSU email for additional safety measures currently in effect and information about available support resources."
The campus initially went into lockdown, but the lockdown has been lifted, according to a university official and VSU police.

The shooting occurred on the same day that resident halls opened to returning students Friday for the school's fall 2026 semester, according to the school's calendar. Classes for the semester will begin on Monday.
Rozia A. Henson Jr., a Democratic member of the Virginia House of Delegates, shared a message on social media praying for the victims and their families.

"Virginia State University is my alma mater. Waking up to this news is heartbreaking. My prayers are with everyone affected this morning, with their families, and with the entire Trojan family. VSU, we are with you," Henson Jr. posted on X.

Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger also addressed the shooting in a social media post Saturday afternoon, saying she and her husband "are praying for a quick recovery for those who were shot this morning at Virginia State University."
"Our thoughts are with the VSU community. Thank you to the first responders and law enforcement who responded to the scene," she wrote.

An investigation into the shooting, led by the Chesterfield County Police Department with assistance from VSU police, U.S. Alcohol Tobacco & Firearms (ATF), and the Hanover County Sheriff's Office, is ongoing, a university official told Fox News Digital.

The university is asking anyone with information to contact Chesterfield County Police at 804-748-1251, Crime Solvers at 804-748-0660, or VSU police at 804-524-5411.

title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial becomes social media obsession as TikTokers, sleuths debate controversial case
summary: Attorney Peter Elikann calls the Lindsay Clancy murder trial a cultural obsession as TikTokers and social media sleuths dissect the controversial case.
story: Boston criminal defense attorney Peter Elikann discussed how the Lindsay Clancy murder trial has become a polarizing topic on social media
The Massachusetts mother at the center of an ongoing murder trial for the killings of her three children is captivating the internet and social media.
"It's kind of a cultural obsession," Boston-based criminal defense attorney Peter Elikann said.

Lindsay Clancy, 35, faces three counts of first-degree murder after her three children, Cora, Dawson and Callan — all under 6 years old — were found strangled to death in the family's Duxbury home in 2023.
POSTPARTUM MOM LINDSAY CLANCY ON TRIAL FOR MURDER BRINGS COURT TO A HALT WITH SUDDEN BREAKDOWN
Defendant Lindsay Clancy listens during her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., July 30, 2026. (CJ Gunther/The Boston Herald via AP, Pool)

She doesn't deny killing them. Clancy and her defense team maintain she was suffering from ongoing postpartum psychosis at the time of their deaths. She entered a plea of not guilty by reason of insanity.
"This isn't a case of having the blues, being down in the dumps and being depressed," Elikann, who is not involved in the trial, told Fox News Digital.
Jurors take a court-supervised view during Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial July 31, 2026. (Josh Reynolds for Daily Mail/Pool; Instagram)
HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL
He explained that the world is just beginning to understand the effects of postpartum psychosis, which differs from postpartum depression.
He referenced the Andrea Yates case from the early 2000s in Houston, Texas, where a mother drowned her five children in a bathtub and was found not guilty by reason of insanity.
"This psychosis is really kind of an emerging field," he says.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
Some TikTokers and social media sleuths are jumping to Clancy's defense, developing conspiracy theories and claiming she did not have the support she needed.

Clancy's attorney is hoping to have one TikToker testify, asking the judge to allow Emily Thorndike, a former McLean Hospital clinical social worker, to be added to the witness list. Thorndike had publicly accused witnesses of spreading "lies and misrepresentations" about the psychiatric center where Clancy was treated weeks before she killed her three children.
Clancy's attorney, Kevin Reddington, said he tracked down Thorndike after she posted about the case on TikTok.
"I saw her video saying that she could not stand for, and I quote, ‘the lies and the misrepresentations from that witness stand about McLean Hospital’," Reddington said.

Speaking about the high interest on social media, Elikann said, "It's kind of a cultural obsession, and people feel that they're part of some kind of community."

title: Killer ex-cop executed for child's slaying as sheriff says he’s sure same monster murdered another girl
summary: James Duckett's execution brought closure to two families who believe the former police officer killed both Teresa McAbee and Jeanifer Weldon in 1987.
story: James Duckett was executed for the 1987 rape and murder of 11-year-old Teresa McAbee. Investigators believe he also killed Jeanifer Weldon that same year. (Credit: WTVT)
After almost four decades, the execution of James Duckett brought closure for two families who believe they both lost young girls to the same killer.
The 68-year-old was executed by lethal injection July 28 for the rape and murder of 11-year-old Teresa McAbee while on duty as a cop for the Mascotte Police Department.
McAbee’s family attended his execution at the Florida State Prison in Raiford.
They were joined by family and friends of 14-year-old Jeanifer Weldon. Authorities believe she also was killed by Duckett four months after he murdered McAbee.
INVESTIGATORS REVISIT FLORIDA SERIAL KILLER CASE AS SEARCH RESUMES FOR POSSIBLE ADDITIONAL VICTIMS
Investigators believe Jeanifer Weldon (L) was killed by James Duckett (R) in Fort Meade, Fla., in September 1987. (Polk County Sheriff’s Office)
But law enforcement officials stopped pursuing a conviction out of fear it would prolong his life, Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said in a news conference.

It had been decided that piecing together evidence on the case could "jam up" the process or "create more defense, or more arguments, or more excuses why he shouldn't be executed," Judd told reporters on July 30.
So once Duckett was sentenced to die for McAbee’s murder, authorities stopped pushing to secure a conviction for the killing of Weldon, Judd said.
Two lives lost
McAbee went missing in May 1987. She was last seen with Duckett in his patrol car on an evening when he was the only officer working the streets.
When her body was found, evidence showed she’d been sexually assaulted, strangled and drowned, according to court records.
A month later, Duckett was named a suspect and was fired from his job as a cop. Very strong fingerprint and DNA evidence linked Duckett to the case, Judd said.
NEW CALIFORNIA LAW EXPANDS DNA TOOLS FOR MISSING PERSONS INVESTIGATIONS
Authorities found Weldon’s body in a wooded area behind the road where her shoes were found. (Polk County Sheriff’s Office)
Then three months later, another girl went missing in Central Florida.
Weldon disappeared on Sept. 19, 1987, in Polk County, about an hour south of the town where Duckett had worked as a police officer.
It was three days before her 15th birthday.
She’d spent the Saturday with friends on a trip to town to Tampa, where she’d bought a fluffy kitten to add to the stuffed animal collection in her bedroom, Judd said.
Around 9 p.m., she left her friends to walk about two miles home, carrying her new stuffed kitten in a green plastic bag, Judd said. She never made it home.

For "13 frantic days, we looked for Jeanifer to no avail," Judd told reporters almost 39 years later. There were few leads, until a phosphate miner pulled over to investigate a pair of shoes he spotted on the side of the road in Fort Meade. It had been about two weeks since Weldon had disappeared.
When he got out of his car, he was hit with the pungent smell of a decomposing body, Judd said.
Weldon’s "skeletonized" remains were found behind tall grass and a berm in a wooded area away from the road, Judd said.
Duckett eventually became a suspect in that killing, too.
Investigators believed Duckett had used his old law enforcement uniform to convince Weldon he could provide a safe ride home.
Family members and investigators felt Weldon wouldn’t have gotten in a car with Duckett without that reassurance and confidence that he was a police officer and someone she could trust, Judd said.
She died by strangulation, he said.
Investigators suspect she was raped before her death.
A heartbreaking clue
A month after Weldon’s death, Duckett was arrested for the killing and sexual battery of McAbee.
He quickly became a suspect in Weldon’s killing, too. But the evidence wasn’t as strong, and was more circumstantial, Judd said.
The night Weldon disappeared, Duckett had left for work at his new mining job five hours early. He drove down the highway "exactly past where Jeanifer Weldon would have been walking home," Judd said.

He arrived at work sweaty and two hours late, saying that he’d had car trouble. But investigators learned that his hands weren't "greasy or nasty or dirty," Judd said. The next day, Duckett brought home a gift for his children—a stuffed kitten in a green plastic bag.
It matched the one purchased by Weldon.
FORENSIC GENEALOGY UNMASKS COLD CASE SUSPECT AS STRANGLER, SEXUAL PREDATOR DECADES LATER: OFFICIALS
Weldon kept a collection of stuffed animals in her bedroom, and her last planned addition provided a clue for investigators looking for her killer. (Polk County Sheriff’s Office)

There also were "fingernail marks or scratches on his back," Judd said. When his wife asked him about the marks, he told her, "I was climbing under a barbed wire fence at work," Judd said. Polk County investigators spent tens of thousands of hours working to pursue a conviction in the Weldon case, Judd said.
Then a few years ago, after Duckett was convicted of McAbee’s murder and had received the death sentence, they questioned whether they should continue pursuing it, he said.

They continued to "chip away" at finding DNA evidence, Judd said. And they hoped Duckett would confess during one of his interviews before his execution.
He declined to talk.
Though he was never convicted of her killing, Duckett’s execution still brought some sense of closure to Weldon’s still-grieving family.
"I'm confident the right person was executed," said Amy Weldon, Jeanifer Weldon’s younger sister. "I don't like how long it took, but I am confident 100% that the right person died."

summary: Larry Montes is facing multiple charges after allegedly striking a congregant and headbutting a security team member during Shabbat services at Central Synagogue in New York City.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A man was charged with multiple hate crimes after allegedly disrupting Shabbat services at a New York City synagogue Friday, striking a congregant and attacking a member of the security team, authorities said.
New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the man disrupted services at Central Synagogue on Lexington Avenue in Manhattan.

The NYPD later identified the suspect as Larry Montes, 46, of the Bronx, and said he was charged with two counts of assault as a hate crime and one count of criminal mischief as a hate crime, among other charges.
NORTH CAROLINA WOMAN CHARGED IN ALLEGED HOUSTON SYNAGOGUE ATTACK PLOT AS INVESTIGATORS SEARCH FOR 2 OTHERS

A Bronx man was charged with multiple hate crimes after allegedly disrupting Shabbat services and attacking a congregant and security member at Central Synagogue in Manhattan, police said. (REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz)

"As synagogue security was escorting him out, he struck a member of the congregation, damaged synagogue property, and then spit at and headbutted a member of the security team," Tisch said in a statement posted on X.
An NYPD sergeant working a paid detail at the synagogue immediately intervened and took Montes into custody, according to Tisch.
No one was seriously injured, and the incident remains under investigation, Tisch said.

"I have spoken with the rabbi of the synagogue, and I'm relieved that no one was seriously injured," she said. "Those who were hurt were evaluated at the scene and are doing well. There are no known additional threats at this time, and additional NYPD resources have been deployed to the synagogue."
JEWISH LEADERS FAULT MAMDANI RHETORIC AS UPPER WEST SIDE STABBING, HATE CRIME PROBE CONTINUES
NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said no one was seriously injured during the alleged attack at Central Synagogue, which she said was the synagogue where she grew up. (WNYW)
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was "horrified" by the incident.
"I am horrified by the assault at Central Synagogue during services today," Mamdani said.

"I can only imagine the pain and fear an attack like this, during Shabbat services, causes for the congregation and for Jewish New Yorkers across our city," he continued. "Every New Yorker must be able to observe their religion without fear of violence."
"This despicable act has no place in our city, and our administration will do everything in our power to keep Jewish New Yorkers safe," he added.
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul also condemned the alleged attack.

"What happened at Central Synagogue tonight is appalling," Hochul posted on X. "Jewish New Yorkers have every right to worship openly, proudly, and without fear. I’m grateful the suspect is in custody and that no one was seriously injured."
Tisch said the incident was particularly personal because she grew up attending Central Synagogue.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was "horrified" by the alleged attack during Shabbat services at Central Synagogue in Manhattan. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

"I understand the sanctity of this space and its meaning for congregants," she said. "Central Synagogue is where I grew up. In joy and in sorrow, it has always been a place of comfort and peace. What happened there tonight is deeply painful. A place of worship should never be a crime scene."

title: Shake Shack worker allegedly calls out before robbing own restaurant, returns in uniform 2 days later
summary: An Arizona Shake Shack employee allegedly robbed his own restaurant at gunpoint, locked co-workers in a cooler, then returned in uniform two days later.
story: A viral video shows a Shake Shack kiosk increasing the price of an order after a customer selected the option to decline a tip. The company responded by attributing the price change to a technology error.

An Arizona Shake Shack employee is facing charges after allegedly robbing his own restaurant at gunpoint, locking two co-workers in a walk-in cooler and then returning to work in uniform just two days later.

Keondre Simmons, 33, allegedly called out of work at the Shake Shack at Kierland Commons in Phoenix around midnight on Aug. 3 before showing up at the restaurant later that morning to commit the robbery, according to court documents reviewed by FOX 10 Phoenix.
Investigators responding to the armed robbery learned that an employee opened a rear delivery door after hearing a bell and believing a scheduled delivery had arrived.
CHICK-FIL-A EMPLOYEE BUSTED IN BIZARRE $80K MAC-AND-CHEESE THEFT SCHEME

Keondre Simmons, 33, is accused of robbing the Shake Shack where he worked at gunpoint before returning to the restaurant in uniform two days later, according to court documents. (Maricopa County Sheriff's Office; iStock)
"[The employee] opened the door after hearing the delivery bell, believing a scheduled delivery had arrived," court documents state.

"When the door opened, the suspect pointed a firearm at [the employee], ordered him inside, and escorted him at gunpoint toward the walk-in cooler. The suspect forced [the employee] inside and locked the cooler door."
Police said the suspect then forced the on-duty manager into the office and ordered him to open the store's safe.

"[The on-duty manager] unlocked the safe and, under threat of firearm, removed approximately $2,800 in mixed denominations and placed it into a black gun case-style container the suspect carried," police wrote. "The suspect subsequently forced [the on-duty manager] into the walk-in cooler with [the employee], and successfully locked the door."
TERRION ARNOLD, LIONS' 2024 FIRST-ROUND PICK, CHARGED WITH KIDNAPPING AND ARMED ROBBERY IN FLORIDA
New York City, USA - April 15, 2013: Customers dine at Shake Shack in Madison Square Park. The chain diner opened in 2004 and the Madison Square Park location is the original. ( )
Investigators said both victims eventually managed to escape the cooler, but the suspect returned moments later, escorted them to the office and ordered them to kneel at gunpoint.

"The suspect took both victims' cellphones and the office landline, then destroyed them by throwing them into a sink filled with water. The suspect then exited the business through the rear delivery door," police wrote.
Investigators later identified Simmons as the suspect, according to the court documents.
Two days after the robbery, Simmons allegedly returned to the Shake Shack wearing his work uniform, where police arrested him.
SIX MEN ALLEGEDLY KIDNAPPED TWO PEOPLE AT VACATION RESORT, TORTURED THEM AT BOAT RAMP: FBI
A Shake Shack employee allegedly stole approximately $2,800 from the restaurant at Kierland Commons in Phoenix after holding two co-workers at gunpoint, according to court documents. (iStock)
Simmons later told investigators that he "discarded the clothing worn during the incident, and a firearm is inside his residence," according to court documents.
Simmons faces charges of armed robbery, aggravated assault and kidnapping.

He is scheduled to appear in court Aug. 25.

title: Delta flight diverted twice after lavatory leak floods cabin, leaves passengers stranded for hours
summary: Delta Air Lines Flight 81 declared an emergency for an overweight landing at Heathrow after a lavatory issue forced the Paris-to-Seattle diversion.
story: A routine maintenance test flight over northwest England drew widespread attention after its flight path appeared to spell out 'I'm bored' on the Flightradar24 flight-tracking website.
A Delta Air Lines flight traveling from Paris to Seattle made an unexpected stop in London after the crew reported a mechanical issue involving an onboard lavatory, the airline said.
Delta Flight 81 departed Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport Aug. 13 bound for Seattle-Tacoma International Airport when the issue prompted the flight crew to divert to London Heathrow Airport.
The Airbus A330-900 was carrying 209 passengers and 13 crew members at the time, according to information provided by Delta.
As the aircraft approached Heathrow, the flight crew declared an emergency with air traffic control because the plane would be making an overweight landing, the airline said.
FLAMES SHOOT FROM AMERICAN AIRLINES FLIGHT BEFORE EMERGENCY LANDING

A Delta Air Lines aircraft taxis at London Heathrow Airport in London Oct. 7, 2016. Delta Flight 81 diverted to Heathrow after its crew reported a mechanical issue involving an onboard lavatory. (Simon Dawson/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Despite the emergency declaration, the aircraft landed normally and safely at Heathrow.
Delta maintenance personnel then serviced the Airbus in London in an effort to address the lavatory-related mechanical issue.

"We apologize to our customers for their experience and delay on Delta Flight 81 from Paris-Charles de Gaulle to Seattle, which diverted to London Heathrow after the crew reported a mechanical issue involving an onboard lavatory," a Delta spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital.
"This is not the experience we strive to provide, and we're focused on getting our customers to their destinations as quickly and safely as possible."
LIVE BULLET FOUND ABOARD UNITED FLIGHT FORCES PASSENGERS OFF PLANE FOR SECURITY SWEEP AT DENVER AIRPORT

A Delta Air Lines Airbus A330-900, registration N812NW, is pictured at Leonardo da Vinci – Fiumicino Airport in Italy July 8, 2025. Delta Flight 81 was operated by an Airbus A330-900 carrying 209 passengers and 13 crew members when it diverted to London. (Massimo Insabato/Archivio Massimo Insabato/Mondadori Portfolio via Getty Images)
Once maintenance work was completed, the aircraft departed Heathrow, but the disruption meant passengers still faced an additional detour before reaching their intended destination on the West Coast.
Instead of continuing directly from London to Seattle, the flight headed to New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport because of the crew's available duty time, according to Delta.
Passengers cleared U.S. Customs at JFK before continuing their journey to Seattle.
The unusual itinerary ultimately took the 209 passengers from Paris to London, then across the Atlantic to New York before they could continue on to Seattle.

Passengers prepare to board a flight at London Heathrow Airport June 27, 2026. Delta Flight 81 made an unscheduled stop at Heathrow while traveling from Paris to Seattle after its crew reported a mechanical issue. (Marc Fernandes/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Delta did not provide additional details about the specific mechanical problem involving the lavatory or what maintenance was required to address it.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: Police reveal new details about gunman, 5 victims killed in rural Michigan shooting rampage
summary: A Missaukee County, Michigan, shooting left six dead across multiple locations as police hunted suspect Chad Hickman, who was considered armed and dangerous.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
State police on Saturday identified the ages of six people, including a suspected gunman, who were killed Friday in rural Missaukee County, Michigan, multi-scene shooting.

On Friday, Michigan State Police (MSP) shared on social media that officers were investigating a shooting in the area that was reported just before noon and that authorities were looking for suspect Chad Hickman, 39, who they said should be considered "armed and dangerous."
In an update on Saturday afternoon, police revealed the ages and genders of the victims.

At around 11:40 a.m. local time Friday, state troopers were dispatched to a home on South LaChance Road in Lake Township, where they found three people who had been killed, including a 45-year-old man, 40-year-old woman and 16-year-old boy.
NEW YORK STATE POLICE LAUNCH MANHUNT AFTER KILLING, HOUSE FIRE FOR 'ARMED AND DANGEROUS' SUSPECT
Shooting suspect Chad Hickman was found dead by police. (Michigan State Police)
In the same home, troopers also found a 13-year-old girl who had been shot, according to MSP.
Authorities said she was taken to the hospital in critical condition. As of Saturday afternoon, she is in stable condition.
During the "large-scale" search for Hickman, police found a fourth body at another home in Missaukee County belonging to a 53-year-old man, authorities said.
State police said Hickman's car was seen near a wooded area where his body, along with the body of a 29-year-old woman were later found.
Police said there is no ongoing danger to the public, and that the investigation remains ongoing.
The names of the victims have not yet been publicly released.
Michigan State Police shared on social media Friday that officers were investigating a shooting in the area and that authorities were looking for the gunman. (Emily Elconin/Getty Images, File)

"Not only is this difficult for our investigators and our troopers, but it's very hard for this community. You know, this type of loss is tragic," MSP public information officer Lt. Ashley Miller told UpNorthLive. "We're going to conduct a thorough investigation. And we want to make sure to keep our community members up to date on our current situation and what we're discovering throughout this process."
Missaukee County is located roughly three hours north of Detroit.

title: FBI captures Top Ten Most Wanted fugitive with alleged Sinaloa Cartel ties, Patel says
summary: Gregory Henderson Jr. was captured three days after being added to the FBI Ten Most Wanted list for alleged drug trafficking tied to the Sinaloa Cartel.
story: Los Angeles Police Department Chief Jim McDonnell says authorities are now offering a $1 million reward for Omar Alexander Cardenas, a suspect on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list. (KTTV)

The FBI captured Ten Most Wanted fugitive Gregory Henderson Jr., just three days after adding the alleged Indianapolis gang leader to its list and offering a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest.

Henderson, 46, had evaded arrest since a sweeping federal takedown of his alleged organization in August 2023. He faces federal charges of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute and to distribute controlled substances, conspiracy to launder monetary instruments and conspiracy to engage in an animal fighting venture.

The FBI alleges Henderson led a violent Indianapolis gang whose drug trafficking network was supplied by the Sinaloa Cartel and distributed methamphetamine, cocaine and fentanyl throughout Indianapolis and the surrounding Midwest.
WOMAN ADDED TO FBI'S TEN MOST WANTED LIST ARRESTED HOURS LATER AFTER TIPS POURED IN FROM FLORIDA: PATEL
The FBI marked Gregory Henderson Jr.’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives poster "CAPTURED" following his arrest. (FBI)

His capture marks the ninth FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive apprehended since President Donald Trump returned to office. The nine fugitives had collectively spent more than 50 years on the run, according to the FBI. The FBI says the nine captures are more than twice the four Ten Most Wanted fugitives captured during the Biden administration.
FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital exclusively that Henderson’s capture reflected a broader increase in Ten Most Wanted apprehensions under the Trump administration.

"Nine Top Ten Most Wanted Fugitives is more than twice as many as captured under the entirety of the prior administration — and this FBI and our partners did it in 18 months under President Trump’s brilliant leadership," Patel said. "Gregory Henderson Jr. had been on the run for a year, wanted for his alleged involvement in major drug trafficking operation and animal fighting conspiracies as the alleged leader of a violent neighborhood-based gang located in Indianapolis, Indiana - a gang with significant drug distribution ties to the Sinaloa Cartel."

"This administration is letting good cops be cops and they are delivering in historic ways. I’d like to congratulate our FBI Indianapolis team who led this case from the beginning and thank our great Justice Department and law enforcement partners who righteously pursued this case with us," he added.
'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN
Gregory Henderson Jr. was captured after being added to the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list on Aug. 11. (FBI)
The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Office of Inspector General was among the federal partners involved in the case.

"I would like to thank the FBI, DOJ, and our USDA OIG among many other federal partners in their relentless pursuit for justice. Mr. Henderson had sought to evade the law after committing multiple crimes and leaving behind pain and anguish for many people and animals, but today is the end of that devastation," U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins told Fox News Digital "President Trump has focused his administration on delivering justice for those targeted by violent crimes, and we will not rest until we achieve this goal."
The FBI added Henderson to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list on Aug. 11, describing him as armed and dangerous.

Henderson and 20 others were federally indicted in the Southern District of Indiana in August 2023 on drug trafficking and dog fighting conspiracy charges. More than 300 federal, state and local law enforcement officers carried out a takedown later that month, arresting 18 people while Henderson evaded capture.
Federal agents seized 61 guns, quantities of fentanyl, methamphetamine and cocaine, $98,000 in cash and 166 fighting dogs during the operation, according to the FBI.
Law enforcement also uncovered what the FBI described as a significant dog fighting and illegal gambling operation allegedly led by Henderson.

"Henderson Jr. has a long history of criminal activity, including street violence, intimidation, assault, and weapons, in addition to drug trafficking and animal cruelty," said FBI Indianapolis Special Agent in Charge Tim O’Malley.

Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel (C) speaks at a news conference at the Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice building on June 23, 2026, in Washington, DC. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Details about where and how Henderson was captured were not immediately available.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: Iran war thrusts Diego Garcia into spotlight as official calls US military base ‘integral’
summary: Diego Garcia supports U.S. carrier strike groups and supply chains after an Iranian strike on Bahrain forced the Pentagon to shift logistics.
story: President Trump threatens to deploy ICE agents to US airports, sparking debate over DHS funding and airport security. This comes as Iran targets a joint US-UK military base in the Indian Ocean with intermediate-range ballistic missiles, demonstrating a significant military capability. Experts discuss the Natanz nuclear facility, missile production, and the need for NATO allies to engage in securing the Strait of Hormuz.

An official with the self-described Chagossian government-in-exile said Sunday that the war with Iran has underscored Diego Garcia’s strategic importance to U.S. forces and Middle East regional stability, with the Pentagon shifting logistics to the remote U.K.-U.S. base in the Indian Ocean after an Iranian strike on a major American installation in Bahrain.

The base, in the southern Chagos Archipelago, has reportedly supported carrier strike groups including the USS Abraham Lincoln, whose forces have conducted air operations and helped enforce the blockade of Iranian ports.

The U.S. military’s wartime logistics network now stretches across a roughly 2,200-mile maritime supply route to Diego Garcia, allowing forces to avoid coastal facilities vulnerable to Iranian attacks but requiring longer shuttle runs and slower replenishment, according to The New York Times.

"That is an inconvenience, but it shows the importance of the base," James Tumbridge, an international lawyer who serves as attorney general for the Chagossian government-in-exile, told Fox News Digital.
UK DEFENSE SHORTFALLS HIGHLIGHTED AS BRITAIN AVOIDS IRAN OFFENSIVE ROLE AMID TRUMP CRITICISM
Diego Garcia is a strategic Indian Ocean base hosting 2,500 US military personnel. (Reuters)
"The base is integral to regional security for the U.K., U.S. and our allies. This latest news emphasizes it."
"Bahrain is a far easier target, so the U.S. change of supply arrangement makes sense," Tumbridge said, adding, "Hopefully the new British PM will not deny the U.S. this change of use."

"It shows the importance of the base and asking a third country for permission is not what the U.S. will want, and so I hope this means Trump will still oppose the handover," Tumbridge went on to say, referring to a proposed agreement that would transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius.

In 2025, the U.K. and Mauritius signed a treaty that would recognize Mauritian sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago while allowing the U.K. to retain control of Diego Garcia for an initial 99-year period.
The British government later put implementation of the agreement on hold amid renewed U.S. concerns over the sovereignty transfer.
STARMER IN 'SEISMIC' CRISIS, UK DEFENSE CHIEF QUITS BEFORE HIGH-STAKES TRUMP NATO SUMMIT
Keir Starmer, leader of Britain's Labour Party, speaks during the Prime Minister's Questions, at the House of Commons in London, Britain November 15, 2023. (UK Parliament/Maria Unger/Handout)

Reports emerged in June that U.S. officials had drafted a proposal to bypass Britain and strike a deal to take control of Diego Garcia, one of several alternatives to then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer's plan to transfer sovereignty to Mauritius.

The first minister of the self-described Chagossian government-in-exile responded that month and said the Chagos Islands were not for sale or "for stealing either," but argued that he "can’t blame" Trump for "looking to secure the military base."
"Trump cannot buy the islands. That suggestion made by some is unhelpful to us all. Only the U.K. can sell the islands, as only the U.K. owns them," Tumbridge also said on Sunday.
"The arguments over sovereignty do not get fixed via a sale, and Mauritius cannot sell them unless the U.K. first gives them away," he added.
"It is not in the U.K.’s interest to sell them. Whether we keep them and continue our support for the U.S. base or we cede them to Mauritius is the choice — my desire is the former."
Mauritius has long claimed sovereignty over the archipelago, a position backed by a 2019 advisory opinion from the International Court of Justice and subsequent U.N. action.

The U.K. government, however, permitted the U.S. to use Diego Garcia for limited defensive operations targeting Iranian missile capabilities in March after initially withholding approval for offensive strikes.
GULF COUNTRIES STRONGLY CONDEMN IRAN'S DRONE ATTACK ON BAHRAIN AS RISING TENSIONS THREATEN MOU

A U.S. B-2 Spirit bomber, part of the 509th Bomb Wing at Whiteman Air Force Base in Missouri, stops for refueling at the U.S. military base on Diego Garcia in October 2001, following an airstrike mission over Afghanistan in support of Operation Enduring Freedom. (U.S. Department of Defense/Senior Airman Rebeca M. Luquin)

"The U.S. wanted to use Chagos Diego Garcia for air strikes at the very beginning. The U.K. consulted Mauritius and refused — hence Trump finally appreciating why sovereignty transfer was a problem," Tumbridge said.
"After the attacks on Cyprus, the U.K. allowed certain so-called defense uses, and Iran did fire at Diego Garcia, but they missed."
On March 20, Reuters reported that Iran had fired two ballistic missiles toward Diego Garcia.

One missile failed in flight, while a U.S. warship fired an interceptor at the other, though it was initially unclear whether the interception succeeded. British officials later said one missile fell short and the other was intercepted.
"No serious concerns have been shared — the earlier attempt showed a lack of range and targeting ability," Tumbridge said.

"The British Government and the Commissioner for the Territory have already tried to say the last attack makes the islands unsafe. No one seriously believes that Iran would try to target the outer islands that presently only have a population of six people."
PENTAGON RACES TO BUY 10X MORE MISSILES AS IRAN WAR DWINDLES ARSENAL, THREATENS READINESS FOR CHINA AGGRESSION
Diego Garcia, the largest island in the Chagos archipelago and site of a major United States military base in the middle of the Indian Ocean, leased from the UK in 1966. (Reuters)
The reported U.S. logistical strains and renewed focus on Diego Garcia came as the USS Abraham Lincoln approached nine months of continuous deployment in the region.
Speaking at Joint Base Andrews on Aug. 14, Trump said a new aircraft carrier was heading to the Middle East to replace it.
"That ship is moving," Trump said when reporters asked about the carrier.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Meanwhile, Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of U.S. Central Command, also met with service members aboard the carrier, which is expected to be relieved amid concerns raised by families over the extended deployment.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the Pentagon for comment.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Bab el-Mandeb Strait faces growing threat as Houthi attacks raise fears of a second Hormuz
summary: Iran-backed Houthis exploit Yemen's fractured state to threaten Bab el-Mandeb, raising fears it could become a second Strait of Hormuz choke point.
story: Tawakkol Karman tells Fox News Digital that restoring the Yemeni state is the only path to lasting peace and countering the Iran-backed Houthis.
The Iran-backed Houthis’ escalating attacks on shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait are raising a growing strategic question: Could the waterway become the next Strait of Hormuz?

The answer is complicated by the geography — and by Yemen itself. Unlike Hormuz, where Iran can directly threaten shipping from its own coastline, Tehran’s leverage over Bab el-Mandeb depends largely on its Houthi allies. And the country overlooking the strait is fractured among competing armed and political forces, leaving the U.S. and its regional allies confronting a threat that may be difficult to solve with naval power alone.

The danger was underscored Tuesday when the Houthis attacked the Egyptian-owned cargo ship Tihamah in Bab el-Mandeb. Four crew members — three Pakistanis and one Indonesian — were killed, according to Yemeni and Pakistani officials, while two Yemeni rescuers were killed when the Houthis struck again after rescue crews arrived, Yemen’s Coast Guard said. Reuters reported that the fatalities, if confirmed, would be the first deaths in a Houthi strike on shipping since the U.S.-Iran war began Feb. 28.
IRAN-BACKED HOUTHI THREAT IN RED SEA COULD LEAD TO MAJOR US POLICY SHIFT, ANALYSTS SAY
Yemeni soldiers patrol the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Yemen, April 5, 2026. (Abdulnasser Alseddik/AP Photo)

The Bab el-Mandeb Strait, is located between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, connects the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea to the Red Sea and, farther north, the Suez Canal and the Mediterranean. It is a crucial route for energy and commercial shipping. The Suez Canal and Egypt’s SUMED pipeline effectively form the northern end of the same Red Sea corridor.
But the southern side of that corridor borders a country that has been at war for more than a decade.

The Houthis control the capital, Sanaa, and much of northern Yemen, while the internationally recognized, Saudi-backed government and an array of allied or competing groups control areas elsewhere. The Southern Transitional Council, a separatist movement that has been backed by the United Arab Emirates, has been a major force in the south.
That fragmentation is becoming increasingly relevant to the security of the waterway.
IRAN-BACKED TERROR PROXY HOUTHIS THREATEN FRESH ATTACKS AFTER YEMEN AIRPORT STRIKE

Amr Al Bidh, the STC’s foreign affairs chief, told Fox News Digital that naval forces can defend individual vessels but cannot by themselves remove the threat posed by Houthi-controlled territory overlooking the maritime route.
"Naval presence protects individual ships. It does not take away Houthi launch sites, it does not interdict the smuggling routes that resupply them and it does not hold terrain," Al Bidh said.
He said that "you have to be on the ground" to ultimately secure Bab el-Mandeb.
Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, on Aug. 3, 2026. (Reuters)

The deterioration comes amid a broader escalation in Yemen. U.N. Special Envoy Hans Grundberg told the Security Council Thursday that the country faces its most serious threat of a return to large-scale war since the U.N.-brokered 2022 truce, warning that renewed Houthi attacks on commercial vessels risk drawing Yemen deeper into the wider regional confrontation.

That truce sharply reduced major fighting after years of war following the Houthis’ seizure of Sanaa in 2014 and the Saudi-led military intervention the following year. Though the formal truce expired in October 2022, large-scale hostilities remained comparatively limited for years.
IRAN BLOCKADE ‘GOING GLOBAL’ IS A WARNING SIGNAL TO CHINA AND RUSSIA

Yemen's Iran-backed armed Houthi group has warned they will move to shutter the Bab Al-Mandeb Strait through missile-drone attacks if Gulf nations join the US-Israel war on Iran. (Mohammed Hamoud/Getty Images)

On July 20, the Houthis declared what they called a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, threatening vessels doing business with Saudi ports. Riyadh denies the Houthi accusation that Saudi Arabia has imposed a siege on Yemen.

A White House official, speaking on background, said the United States expects the Houthis to continue to uphold the terms of the ceasefire. The official said the Houthis "saw during Operation Rough Rider that the United States and President Trump will take necessary action to protect freedom of navigation and U.S. commercial shipping from Houthi terrorist attacks."

The official added that the United States is focused on protecting core national security interests — including freedom of navigation in the Red Sea — while "empowering our regional partners to take the lead in managing and resolving regional security challenges." The official said Washington is in continuous dialogue with Saudi Arabia and the Republic of Yemen government regarding regional stability.

United Against Nuclear Iran, citing Joint Maritime Information Center data, has put the decline in tanker transits since the July 20 blockade declaration at roughly 40%. UANI also said tankers have been observed broadcasting messages including "CHINESE OWNER" and "ARMED GUARD ON BOARD" through their tracking systems, apparently in an effort to reduce the chance of being targeted.
TRADE VESSEL STRUCK BY PROJECTILE IN STRAIT OF HORMUZ AMID US-IRAN TALKS

Thousands of people gather at Sabeen Square, under the control of the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, to protest the killing of Iran’s supreme leader in U.S. and Israeli airstrikes on Iran, in Sanaa, Yemen on March 6, 2026. (Mohammed Hamoud/Anadolu via Getty Images)

China, meanwhile, has been in contact with the Houthis over safe passage for Chinese vessels, according to a July 28 Reuters report citing Chinese and regional sources. Four China-bound tankers had crossed Bab el-Mandeb following the blockade announcement as Beijing sought assurances for its shipping.
The economic stakes are rising because of what is happening hundreds of miles to the east.
Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on its Red Sea export infrastructure as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted by the U.S.-Iran conflict.
That makes the Red Sea both an alternative to Hormuz — and a potential second pressure point.
Yemeni Nobel Peace Prize laureate Tawakkol Karman warned at the United Nations Thursday that Yemen’s internal collapse is increasingly threatening interests far beyond its borders.

"This is no longer a Yemeni crisis alone," Karman said. "The continued collapse of the state in Yemen threatens international navigation and trade, energy security, and global supply chains and undermines regional and international peace and security."

Karman had been invited by Denmark, which holds the Security Council presidency, to brief council members, but Denmark’s deputy U.N. ambassador said "strong opposition" prevented the briefing from taking place. Karman instead addressed reporters outside the chamber.
In a separate interview with Fox News Digital, Karman argued that restoring a functioning Yemeni state is ultimately essential to defeating armed groups and securing the country.
TRUMP WARNS IRAN FIGHTING ISN'T OVER AS HE VOWS US WILL 'WIN' AS TALKS FADE

Houthi terrorists walk over British and U.S. flags at a rally in support of Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, and Houthi strikes on shipping in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden on Feb. 4, 2024, on the outskirts of Sana'a, Yemen. (Mohammed Hamoud/Getty Images)
"Yemeni people can do that," Karman said of defeating the Houthis and other militias. "We can be partners on saving the global and regional security."
"Without restoring Yemen, that means there is not any sustainable peace," she added.
But U.S. experts caution against treating Bab el-Mandeb as simply a second Hormuz.

"Iran doesn’t have the same direct influence on flows through the Bab al-Mandeb as it does for the Strait of Hormuz," Richard Goldberg, a senior advisor at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies and former National Security Council official, told Fox News Digital.
"The strategy would depend much more on proxies — Iraqi groups focusing fire on infrastructure and the Houthis focusing on the Red Sea," Goldberg said.

But he said there are limits to that strategy. "The Houthis act much more independently than they used to, and have not yet shown an interest to going to war against the world — just against Riyadh," Goldberg said.
He also pointed to one critical difference between the two waterways: ships that cannot safely cross Bab el-Mandeb can bypass the Red Sea entirely by sailing around Africa.
"Unlike Hormuz, shippers can go around the Red Sea if they really need to," Goldberg said. "It adds cost and time but it’s not a single point of failure like Hormuz."
The question facing U.S., Saudi Arabia and its partners is therefore how to prevent the Houthi threat from becoming more serious.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, left, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, center, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif sign a defense agreement in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, on Aug. 7, 2026. (TUR Presidency/Murat Cetinmuhurdar/Handout/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Riyadh is now trying to assemble two overlapping layers of regional security cooperation.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement on Aug. 7, a mutual-defense pact that calls for high-level political and military coordination, joint exercises and deeper defense-industry cooperation. Turkey has stressed that the agreement is defensive and does not identify Iran or any other country as an enemy.

Dr. Aziz Alghashian, a Saudi foreign-policy researcher and senior non-resident fellow at Gulf International Forum, told Fox News Digital earlier this week that one immediate implication could be greater coordination against Iran-backed groups, particularly the Houthis.

Alghashian said the pact could produce a greater trilateral presence near the Saudi-Yemeni border, "especially in the maritime dimension," while allowing Riyadh to take a firmer collective approach toward Iran-backed militias even as it maintains a more diplomatic approach toward Tehran itself.
Separately, Saudi Arabia is leading an effort specifically focused on the waterways.

The Saudi Defense Ministry announced July 30 plans for a multinational maritime-defense coalition intended to protect freedom of navigation and commercial and energy routes through Bab el-Mandeb, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Fourteen countries, including Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt, Sudan and Djibouti, initially backed the initiative.
Turkey’s Defense Ministry confirmed Thursday that Ankara is participating in meetings in Jeddah aimed at establishing the coalition.
Ships are anchored in the Strait of Hormuz on Aug. 10, 2026, off the coast of Bandar Abbas, Iran. (Ali Saeedi/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

A State Department spokesperson separately told Fox News Digital that protecting commercial shipping through both the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz remains a "top priority" for the Trump administration, pointing to freedom of navigation as one of Washington’s core national security interests in the Middle East. "We will continue to work with international partners to deter Iranian and Iranian-proxy attacks on merchant vessels, ensure the free flow of commerce and hold accountable those who threaten the safety of international shipping lanes," a State Department spokesperson said.

The spokesperson said the administration is also seeking to disrupt the flow of Iranian money and weapons to the Houthis, noting that the U.S. has sanctioned more than 200 entities associated with the group.

"We condemn Iran’s flagrant violation of Yemen’s sovereignty and international law in threatening freedom of navigation and supporting their Houthi proxies," the spokesperson said. The State Department also emphasized Washington’s support for Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s internationally recognized government as the threat around Bab el-Mandeb grows.

"The United States stands firmly with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognized government of Yemen against Houthi terrorism," the spokesperson said. "We are in close consultation with our Saudi and Yemeni partners and remain committed to their security."

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Exclusive: Israel seizes vast Iran terror axis arsenal with surprising foreign origins
summary: The IDF Tzrifin Base in Central Israel stores a massive arsenal seized from Hezbollah and Hamas, including Iranian rockets, drones and Nazi-era guns.
story: Fox News Digital got rare access to rockets, drones, sniper rifles and other weapons seized from the terror groups, including Iranian-made arms. (Video: IDF.)

JERUSALEM — Fox News Digital gained rare access to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) Tzrifin Base in Central Israel, where a vast number of confiscated rockets, grenades, drones, sniper rifles, automated weapons, anti-tank rocket launchers, mortars and other military firepower used by Hezbollah and Hamas are stored.

The seized arsenal of weapons, ranging in manufacturers from the Islamic Republic of Iran to Russia, China to homegrown producers in Lebanon and Gaza and even a Nazi-era gun, were part of the war machinery used by Hamas and Hezbollah against Israeli civilians and the IDF since Hamas terrorists attacked southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023.
The IDF said Hezbollah also used weapons against Lebanese civilians.
Hezbollah and Hamas, members of Iran’s so-called "axis of resistance," have killed over 300 American citizens, according to reports.
'WE WANT LAND INVASION': IRAN MOUTHPIECE TOUTS NEW MISSILE, BOASTS DECADES OF WAR PREP
PK machine guns used by Hezbollah in Lebanon and seized by the IDF. (IDF)

The Jewish state fought a multi-front war against Iran and its proxies at the height of the conflict. The remains of Iranian rockets litter the ground outside the weapons storage facility at Tzrifin for journalists to inspect.

Tehran fired rockets into civilian areas during the war, including large cities such as Tel Aviv and Be’ersheva. Just days after the joint U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran in late February, the Islamic Republic fired a ballistic missile into Be’ersheva, causing injuries to 19 people.
To the ordinary eye, it is a Herculean challenge to decipher the small Nazi swastika emblem on the German World War II-era MG 34 machine gun seized at a Hezbollah terrorist compound in Lebanon.
But, for the Israeli military commander of the Captured Equipment Evacuation Unit, Lt. Col. (res.) Idan Sharon-Kettler, it is a run-of-the-mill exercise in weapons identification.
The German MG 34 has the "markings of an eagle carrying a swastika stamped on it," Sharon-Kettler said.
IRAN REAFFIRMS SUPPORT FOR HAMAS AS TRUMP PUSHES TO DISARM TERROR GROUP

Sharon-Kettler told Fox News Digital the Nazi machine gun was used as "propaganda or for morale" of the Iranian regime-backed terrorists in Lebanon. A second Nazi-era assault rifle was confiscated from Hezbollah— the MP 44 (also termed StG 44).

Hamas and Hezbollah, both of whom are designated terrorist organizations by the U.S., employed sophisticated methods to transform vehicles into high-intensity offensive weapons. So-called dual-use technology (equipment that can be used for civilian and military purposes) is the bread and butter of Hamas and Hezbollah.

"Motorcycles like these took Israelis hostages," Sharon-Kettler said as he showed an Egyptian Halawa Motors motorcycle that was captured in Israel on Oct. 7. The Iranian regime-backed Hamas terrorist movement killed over 1,200 people on Oct. 7, including more than 40 American citizens. Hamas took over 250 people hostage on the same day.
The IDF also captured rockets from Palestinian Islamic Jihad that were used as "propaganda dummies" during parades against Israel in Gaza.
HAMAS SAYS IT WILL DISSOLVE GAZA GOVERNMENT, BUT ISRAEL WARNS GROUP STILL SEEKS HEZBOLLAH-STYLE CONTROL
Egyptian Halawa Motors motorcycles captured in Israel on Oct. 7. Motorcycles of this type were used to take hostages in Hamas-controlled Gaza. (IDF)
The IDF seized ATVs used by Hezbollah in Lebanon to hold rockets and terrorists. One captured ATV was designed to hold six rockets with launchers.
"You can sit on top of a hill and control a road that goes underneath. And with six anti-tank rockets, you will stop almost any vehicle that passes," Sharon-Kettler said.
He said the ATVs provide great utility for Hezbollah in the rugged, hilly landscape of southern Lebanon.
Iranian-produced mortars were also on display at the IDF base.

"We found hundreds" of mortars in Lebanon, Sharon-Kettler said. The IDF captured drones, including decay drones. Sharon-Kettler said some of the Hezbollah drones are used "to make noise … to divert [IDF]resources."
According to Sharon-Kettler, the IDF captured "dozens" of Iranian regime-produced canons in south Lebanese villages, where Hezbollah’s core base exists.
"In many houses the canons were pointing out of windows," said Sharon-Kettler. One cannon seized in Lebanon originated in Russia.
NETANYAHU REJECTS BOARD OF PEACE'S GAZA PLAN: NO 'WITHDRAWAL UNTIL HAMAS IS GENUINELY DISARMED'
Uniforms made in Syria, China and Lebanon and used by Hezbollah terrorists. (IDF)

Hezbollah, like its counterpart Hamas in Gaza, embeds its terrorists in residential areas and civilian buildings, including hospitals, schools and mosques. The IDF storage site was packed with Russian-produced AK-47 automatic rifles and various versions of it.
The IDF captured more recent Russian AK-103 and AK-104 automatic rifles in southern Lebanon.
"Light sniper rifles, some made in Iran, some Russian, are very common with Hezbollah and Hamas," Sharon-Kettler said.

Israel’s army also seized a highly decorated Turkish hunting rifle that was used by Hezbollah. The IDF found many highly sophisticated Austrian Steyr sniper rifles, including the Austrian Steyr HS .50 caliber sniper rifle, in possession of Hezbollah. Sharon-Kettler showed an Iranian replicated version of the Steyr sniper rifle.
The IDF collected submachine guns in Lebanon that were manufactured by China and Russia and anti-tank launchers produced by Russia and Iran, the IDF weapons expert said.
A Hezbollah drone seized by the IDF. (IDF)

Additional merchandise seized by the IDF includes all the trappings of a professional army and guerrilla terrorist forces. Well-crafted uniforms made in Syria, China and Lebanon along with helmets, anti-shrapnel vests and medical kits are part of the IDF's confiscated war equipment.
Sharon-Kettler explained the reasons for Israel being in Lebanon.

"Even after the agreement we had with the Lebanese army and government, once we entered Lebanon again, we kept finding everything that is here. For me, it means, if we are not doing the work to clean Lebanon from military entities targeting are civilians, nobody else is doing that."
The IDF commander referred to the November 2024 ceasefire agreement reached between Lebanon and Israel to cease the war between Jerusalem and the Hezbollah terrorist organization.
Hezbollah joined Hamas in its war on Israel Oct. 8, 2023
