Maher Assad was a former commander of the Syrian military’s 4th Armored Division — which Syrian opposition activists have accused of killings, torture, extortion and drug trafficking, in addition to running its own detention centers.

title: Israel vindicated by Gaza nutrition data after ‘blood libel’ starvation claims, UN envoy says
summary: A United Nations-backed survey found no widespread acute malnutrition in Gaza, prompting Israel's ambassador to call prior famine claims a blood libel.
story: Danny Danon, Israeli UN envoy says new Gaza nutrition findings expose

Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations said new data showing sharply lower child malnutrition in Gaza undermines wartime accusations that Israel deliberately starved Gazans, calling those claims a "blood libel" fueled by Hamas figures.

The remarks by Ambassador Danny Danon follow a newly published U.N.-backed survey showing acute malnutrition among young children in the Gaza Strip has dropped to levels comparable to or below those recorded prior to the outbreak of the Israel-Hamas war.

"During the war in Gaza, Israel was accused by many countries and by many U.N. officials that we deliberately starved the population in Gaza. That was a blood libel," Danon told Fox News Digital. "When we actually answered those claims and asked our colleagues where they got the data, the answer was that they relied on Hamas reports."
Danon argued that the latest U.N.-backed figures undermine previous starvation claims and said earlier numbers attributed to Hamas were fabricated.
SURVIVOR OF HAMAS TERROR ATTACK IN ISRAEL SLAMS MAMDANI OVER 'DANGEROUS' VIDEO ABOUT NETANYAHU
Hamas terrorists carrying clubs and firearms secure and divert humanitarian aid trucks in the northern Gaza area of Jabaliya on June. 25. (TPS-IL)

"For the future, we shouldn't count on a terrorist organization. We are a reliable country, we share data, we share concerns regarding humanitarian issues, and we should not collaborate with terrorists," he said.

The Gaza SMART nutrition survey — coordinated by the UNICEF-led Nutrition Cluster and presented by the State of Palestine Nutrition Cluster on July 22, 2026 — evaluated 1,335 children under age 5, covering regions home to approximately 83% of Gaza's population.
About 17% of the population could not be surveyed due to security and operational constraints.
The survey found acute malnutrition rates between 0.2% and 0.8% using weight-for-height (WHZ) measurements (estimated globally at 0.5%) and 1.3% using mid-upper-arm circumference (MUAC).
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROBES UNRWA OVER ALLEGED EMPLOYMENT OF 1,500 TERRORISTS
A truck carrying aid is standing in front of the Rafah crossing, waiting to enter the Gaza Strip on January 13, 2026, in Rafah, Egypt. (Ali Moustafa/Getty Images)

Evaluators concluded there was "no widespread acute malnutrition at population level," noting that rates are significantly lower than those in neighboring countries, though lingering challenges like stunting, poor diet diversity and illness remain.
Danon pointed directly to past statements made by senior international officials, including U.N. Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher.

During a 2025 BBC interview about border access, Fletcher said 14,000 babies were at risk of dying within 48 hours without immediate nutritional aid. The figure was later clarified as referring to an 11-month projection involving children at risk of severe malnutrition.
"That was false and did not happen. Using starvation and babies to spread blood libels against Israel is outrageous," Danon said of Fletcher's comments.
"We care about babies in Gaza more than those making these allegations against us."
The ambassador emphasized that Israel kept records of food supplies moving into the enclave throughout the conflict.
"In terms of the food coming into Gaza, that was very easy for us to prove because we control the checkpoints and count the number of trucks coming in," Danon explained.
ISRAEL ACCUSES UN OF PLACING IT ON SAME SEXUAL VIOLENCE BLACKLIST AS HAMAS TERRORISTS, SEVERS TIES

Israeli U.N. Ambassador Danny Danon issued a scathing letter in response to U.N. Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher's remarks before the Security Council. (Getty Images)

"We know what they carry. Thus, we know there is no lack of food entering Gaza, and we always ensure sufficient supplies are brought in. Looking at recent reports, the situation is much better than expected, and we are glad for that. We do not want to see famine anywhere in the world, and certainly not in our backyard."
Danon also accused Hamas of hijacking aid distribution networks for financial gain.

"We know for a fact that Hamas took the aid and sold it in the market, taking advantage of the situation with inflated prices," he said. "That is why we are trying to work with NGOs that are not infiltrated by Hamas. We want NGOs to be able to deliver aid and food without Hamas gaining control over it."
IRAN REAFFIRMS SUPPORT FOR HAMAS AS TRUMP PUSHES TO DISARM TERROR GROUP
Hamas terrorists in the northern Gaza Strip on Dec. 1, 2025. (Omar Al-Qatta / AFP via Getty Images)
Israel withdrew its military and civilian presence from the Gaza Strip in 2005.
The war broke out following Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attack on southern Israel and continued for two years until a ceasefire agreement took effect on Oct. 10, 2025.
Now, the region continues to face military strikes as talks over a proposed 15-point U.S. peace and disarmament plan appear stalled.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected the proposal, saying Israeli forces will not withdraw until Hamas is fully disarmed.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Unfortunately, Hamas took over and turned it into a terror state," Danon said.
"Our vision remains unchanged: we have no desire to control Gaza. However, for progress to occur, Hamas must disarm and not move weapons from one warehouse to another."

"Regarding the food situation, we see improvement on the ground," Danon concluded. "The prices in the markets in Gaza have gone down dramatically, which serves as the clearest indicator that there is no food shortage."

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Trump orders military to ‘substantially reduce’ joint exercises with South Korea
summary: The president said he has directed the Pentagon to scale down the exercises, citing South Korea’s refusal to join the war in Iran and his “very good” relationship with North Korea’s Kim Jong Un.
story: President Donald Trump said Sunday that he has directed the Defense Department to scale down joint military exercises with South Korea, citing the U.S. ally’s refusal to join the war in Iran and his “very good” relationship with North Korea’s Kim Jong Un.

Trump said the large, annual military drills sent a “signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile” to North Korea, a country with which the U.S. has no formal diplomatic ties but which Trump says has been “unthreatening and respectful” as long as he has been president.
“Based on the fact that it is too late to cancel, I have instructed Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, to substantially reduce the Joint Military Exercises!” Trump wrote on social media.
Kim Jong Un rides a tank driven by his teenage daughter
Trump also mentioned South Korea’s refusal to join the Iran war.

“While somewhat unrelated (?), I recently asked the President of South Korea if they would like to join us in the Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and they said, ‘No thanks!’” Trump wrote.
It was not immediately clear what a scaled-down version of the training, set to start Monday only hours after Trump’s announcement, would look like.
The South Korean defense ministry said Monday that the drills, known as Ulchi Freedom Shield and scheduled to last until Aug. 27, were “proceeding as planned.”

According to U.S. Forces Korea, the exercises are meant to build understanding among several agencies to ensure “their ability to fortify the combined defense posture and enhance Alliance response capabilities against a spectrum of security threats.” North Korea routinely criticizes the annual drills as a “war rehearsal,” which the U.S. and its allies deny, and threatens to retaliate.
South Korea’s embassy in Washington and U.S. Forces Korea did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Trump’s announcement comes days after North Korea launched a ballistic missile toward the sea, conducting weapons testing in possible protest of the upcoming U.S.-South Korea military drills.

It also comes a day after the U.S. pulled its last aircraft carrier in Asia, as the USS George Washington was sent to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln — which has drawn scrutiny over conditions on board — in the Persian Gulf.

title: Actor Hayden Panettiere, known for roles in ‘Heroes,’ ‘Nashville,’ dies at 36
summary: The cause and manner of death were unclear. Panettiere revealed this year that she struggled with postpartum depression and addiction, which she said led to her decision to give up custody of her daughter in 2018.
story: Actor Hayden Panettiere has died, her father said in a statement Sunday night. She was 36.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden,” her father, Skip Panettiere, said in a statement provided by her representative.
The cause and manner of death were not provided. Her publicist, Kasey Kitchen, said Panettiere’s death was being investigated.
“There’s an investigation ongoing,” Kitchen said in a statement. “We should know more tomorrow.”

Panettiere revealed this year that she struggled with postpartum depression and addiction, which she said led to her decision to give up custody of her only child, daughter Kaya Evdokia Klitschko, in 2018, whom she had with former partner Wladimir Klitschko, the Ukrainian professional boxer.
Panettiere recently published a memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” which generated headlines over its revelations, including about her past relationships.
In 2024, she described pain and grief after her younger brother, actor Jansen Panettiere, died unexpectedly of an undiagnosed heart condition the previous year.
“When you lose somebody that you saw in all the important moments in your life, standing right next to you, it just rocks your world,” she told NBC’s “TODAY” show.
The actor was born and raised in Palisades, New York, about 40 miles north of New York City, according to her Television Academy bio.
Panettiere started working at 11 months old, when she appeared in television commercials, it said.

She appeared on soap operas, including “One Life to Live” and “Guiding Light,” beginning at age 4. Her voice was featured in “A Bug’s Life,” the animated feature, and she eventually appeared in big-screen stories, including “Remember the Titans” and “Bring It On: All or Nothing.”
One of her most impactful roles was as Juliette Barnes on television’s “Nashville.” Before that, she was Claire Bennet on the 2000s show “Heroes.”
Her time shooting “Nashville” included the pressure of having had a baby and experiencing postpartum depression, she said, and at times it was too much.

title: Here’s the biggest news you missed this weekend
summary: Plus, a major-league pitcher whose groundbreaking surgery extended the careers of MLB greats dies at 83.
story: One person was killed in a storm-related car crash as Hurricane Lala imposed fierce wind and pouring rain on Hawaii’s Big Island, Gov. Josh Green said.
Hurricane Lala hits Hawaii's Big Island with heavy rains

Honolulu Fire Chief Sheldon Hao said first responders responded to reports Saturday of damaged roofs and downed trees. More than 130,000 utility customers in the state were without electricity Sunday morning.

Lala just avoided making landfall on the Big Island, which hasn’t had a direct hit from a hurricane in 155 years. Parts of the Big Island and Maui reported about a foot of rain, the National Hurricane Center said.

Extreme weather was also affecting Indiana, where at least six people died in a powerful storm system, officials said. Severe flooding inundated communities and strained emergency services across the state.
‘Meet the Press’

Attorney General Todd Blanche said Sunday there’s a “possibility” the Justice Department will ask the Supreme Court to intervene in dozens of cases in which judges have ruled against the federal government’s efforts to gain broad access to state voter rolls ahead of November’s midterm elections.
“Absolutely it’s a possibility,” Blanche told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” when he was asked whether he would appeal the 22 cases the Justice Department has lost so far to the Supreme Court.
“Election integrity is something that President Trump ran on, and the American people elected him. It’s something that every American should care about,” Blanche said.

The cases stem from an executive order Trump signed directing states to turn over voter rolls, including voters’ names, dates of birth, residential addresses, state driver’s license information and the last four digits of their Social Security numbers. The federal government says it’s collecting the data so the Justice Department can investigate “deficiencies” or “anomalies,” including whether noncitizens are registered to vote.
While some states have voluntarily complied with the administration’s request, the Justice Department has sued 30 states and Washington, D.C., over their refusal to turn over the data.

Blanche also said that it wouldn’t be ideal for the FBI to take over the investigation into the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie in Arizona but that federal investigators are providing as much help as possible.Rep. Democrats set 2028 primary calendar, with South Carolina going first

Democrats teed up South Carolina to lead a six-state gantlet of early presidential contests, sealing a 2028 road map that pushes Black and Latino voters and labor to the front of the line to choose the party’s next national leader.

After discussions Saturday in Texas, the Democratic National Committee formally selected South Carolina, with its large African American primary electorate, as the first-in-the-nation state. It will be followed by Nevada, with high numbers of Latinos and powerful labor interests. Next up are New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and then Virginia.
Officials in Iowa and New Hampshire expressed frustration after they were bucked from their decadeslong spots at the front of the pack, with one calling it “disappointing.”
Former MLB pitcher Tommy John dies at 83

Tommy John, the longtime major-league baseball pitcher whose name is forever linked to the groundbreaking elbow surgery that saved his career and the careers of countless others since, has died, officials said Sunday. He was 83.
John will best be known for his years with the Los Angeles Dodgers and the New York Yankees, two of the sport’s most famed franchises.

“Tommy was an exceptional pitcher throughout his career in Major League Baseball, and his courageous role in becoming the first to have surgery that would go on to bear his name can’t be overstated,” Dodgers President Stan Kasten said in a statement.

In a farewell note to Yankees owners and staff members posted this month, John thanked the doctor who saved his career with an operation to repair a torn ligament in his elbow, noting that the surgery has saved the careers of some of the game’s best pitchers.
‘Revenge is inevitable’: Iran ramps up propaganda war with violent billboards

The billboards are state-sponsored, plastered across Iran’s capital and far from subtle. One features an image of Trump lying in a casket; another shows the White House on fire; a third is a parody of the American flag with skulls in place of the stars and bombs dropping from the stripes.

Alongside ads for a multitude of products such as cars and shampoo, the giant billboards have become familiar sights to the people of Tehran in recent years. But since the country’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was killed in an airstrike on the first day of the war launched by the U.S. and Israel, the messaging has become bolder and the tone more violent.
The modern images also appear to have been generated with the help of artificial intelligence, which Iran has used to boost its online propaganda efforts throughout the war.

title: Woman leaps from 11th-floor ledge into firefighter’s arms as Berlin high-rise burns
summary: As a furious blaze raged inside a high-rise apartment building in Berlin, one woman was rescued by scaling the building’s exterior and taking a terrifying leap more than two stories down to safety.
story: As a furious blaze raged inside a high-rise apartment building in Berlin, one woman was rescued by scaling the building’s exterior and taking a terrifying leap more than two stories down to safety.
The fire erupted in an 18-story residential high-rise building in the German capital’s Friedrichshain neighborhood around 6:30 a.m. Friday, The Associated Press reported.

The blaze started in an apartment on the 11th floor and spread to the apartment above it, with flames shooting from several windows and thick, black smoke pluming from the building, Berlin police said.

The dramatic rescue, captured on video, shows a woman in sweatpants scaling the exterior of an 11th-floor apartment, edging perilously along a window ledge as giant orange flames and black smoke billow from the apartment beside her.
Two floors below her outside, a firefighter is seen in the basket of a turntable ladder used for elevated rescues.

She spends several tense minutes trying to climb down to the apartment below, but can’t find footing. Finally, she lets go of the ledge and takes a heart-stopping leap, falling into a rescue basket held by the firefighter, who catches her.

Police said the woman, who was not identified, jumped roughly two floors down into the basket and was safely caught. She sustained minor injuries and was taken to a hospital for treatment, police said.

In total, the fire affected 115 people. Twenty-five were rescued or brought to safety via fire-escape hoods on the stairwell and a turntable ladder, police said. Thirteen people suffered minor injuries and received emergency medical treatment, with some transported to nearby hospitals for further care.
Authorities described the response as “especially strenuous and requiring a significant number of personnel” given the number of people affected and the scale of the fire.
Eighteen fire engines, two aerial ladder trucks, nine ambulances and more were deployed to quell the blaze and carry out rescues. The cause of the fire is not yet known.

title: Former MLB pitcher Tommy John dies at age 83
summary: Tommy John, the longtime Major League baseball pitcher whose name is forever linked to the groundbreaking elbow surgery that saved his career and those of countless others since, has died, officials said Sunday.
story: Tommy John, the longtime Major League baseball pitcher whose name is forever linked to the groundbreaking elbow surgery that saved his career and those of countless others since, has died, officials said Sunday.
He was 83.
John is survived by his wife and three children, Tommy, Travis and Tamara, according to a statement from the Los Angeles Dodgers, one of the southpaw’s six major league teams.
John had been in hospice care, Reuters reported last week.

“Tommy was an exceptional pitcher throughout his career in Major League Baseball, and his courageous role in becoming the first to have surgery that would go on to bear his name can’t be overstated,” Dodgers President Stan Kasten said in a statement.
“His impact both on and off the field has been felt by ballplayers of all ages and will be for generations to come,” Kasten said.
John will be best known for years with the Dodgers and New York Yankees, two of the sports’s most famed franchises.
He skipped last weekend’s annual Old-Timers’ Day event at Yankee Stadium and issued a statement, announcing his retirement from public life.
He expressed gratitude to Yankees owners and staff in his farewell, as well as to the doctor who saved his career with a surgery to repair a torn ligament in his elbow.

“That surgery has since gone on to save the careers of countless pitchers, including may of the very best in the game today,” John wrote. “Thank you to all the fans who supported me & my teammates for 26 years. I will never forget you.”

The Yankees released a statement following John’s death describing him as a “bedrock” of the team’s pitching rotation and a favorite among the fans. It went on to note that the story of John’s famed surgery overshadowed his work on the mound, which included consecutive 20‑win seasons with the Yankees.

“We pause to remember the totality of his legacy — his competitiveness and skill, his penchant for conversation, his kind and gracious nature, and his stature as an athletic and medical pioneer,” the team said.

John’s MLB career began with a short stint in Cleveland in 1963 before he was traded to the Chicago White Sox before the 1965 campaign. He was playing on the Los Angeles Dodgers in 1974 when a torn ulnar collateral ligament in his elbow blew his season.

Dr. Frank Jobe, the team’s doctor at the time, performed a surgery to replace the ligament with a tendon from elsewhere in his body. The procedure had never been performed before and was revolutionary at the time.
That surgery is now named after the pitcher, who became known as the “Bionic Man” following a thrilling return from what should have been a career-ending injury.

John told The New York Times in 1977 that he spent the entire 1975 season rebuilding strength in his arm. He worked with team trainer Bill Buhler, soaked his arm and even squeezed Silly Putty to help regain his strength.
“I put together three of those Silly Putty eggs,” John said. “Bill Buhler told me that Silly Putty was better than a rubber ball because I could squeeze all the way through it.”
It would be two years before John would finally return to the Dodgers rotation, making 31 starts and managing two shutouts in his 1976 comeback season.
He recorded the first of his three 20-win seasons in 1977, helping the Dodgers to the National League pennant that year.
He had another solid year in 1978, as L.A. won another NL flag, before signing a free agent deal that ensuing winter to join the Yankees, who had beaten the Dodgers in consecutive World Series.

title: Todd Blanche says FBI will continue providing assistance on Nancy Guthrie investigation but doesn’t have any updates
summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche said he doesn’t believe it would be the best course of action for the FBI to take over the investigation into the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie in Arizona
story: Attorney General Todd Blanche said Sunday that he doesn’t believe it would be the best course of action for the FBI to take over the investigation into the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie in Arizona but added that federal investigators are providing as much help as possible.

“We are working as hard as we can with the state and local law enforcement in every area, and that means not only providing assistance with manpower, but any sort of forensic assistance,” Blanche told NBC News’ “Meet the Press.” “And so we’re going to continue to do that. Whether we come in with sharp elbows and take it over, that’s not necessarily the right thing to do for her or for anybody, but making sure that it’s done right and making sure that this investigation is being conducted the way that it should be is something that we’re doing.”
Nancy Guthrie, the mother of “TODAY” show co-anchor Savannah Guthrie, was first reported missing on Feb. 1 in Tucson, Arizona, in a case that has drawn national attention.

Nancy Guthrie has remained missing since then, and authorities in Pima County have publicly offered few concrete leads in their investigation. Early on, national and local authorities deemed the case an abduction, and videos released by the FBI from Guthrie’s doorbell camera showed a masked and armed man outside her home shortly before she disappeared.

Earlier this month, The Wall Street Journal reported that local and state authorities have continued to lead the case since it was opened in February, with the FBI assisting in certain areas as needed.
In February, just days after her mother’s disappearance, President Donald Trump spoke with Guthrie to offer every available form of assistance from federal law enforcement.

“I spoke with Savannah Guthrie, and let her know that I am directing ALL Federal Law Enforcement to be at the family’s, and Local Law Enforcement’s, complete disposal, IMMEDIATELY,” the president wrote in a Truth Social post at the time.

On Sunday, Blanche said that he did not have an update on the investigation to share publicly, adding: “I’m sorry to say that because I wish I had an update, and I know that this type of case is heartbreaking, especially when it plays out nationally like this one has.”

title: Rep. Ro Khanna calls for ‘Data Center Bill of Rights’ and says the industry needs regulation
summary: The California congressman also laid out how he believes he differs from Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, as both progressives are floated as potential presidential candidates.
story: Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., called for a “Data Center Bill of Rights,” arguing in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press” that data centers needed to be regulated so local communities have a larger say on where to build them.

Earlier this month, Khanna introduced a Data Center Bill of Rights resolution laying out a series of suggested guardrails on data centers, which have become a prominent issue in elections across the country.

Asked by moderator Kristen Welker whether the U.S. could lead the world in artificial intelligence if it opposes data center infrastructure, Khanna argued that “you can’t shove a data center down the throats of a local community without any say that that community has.”
“You can’t be jacking up electricity prices,” he said. “Even the technology leaders understand that there needs to be a pause so that we can get this right.”
Asked to clarify that he was not opposed to data centers but believes they need to be regulated, Khanna said, “I believe it needs regulation.”
“I introduced a Data Center Bill of Rights, saying it should never be in a residential community or farmland, and a local community should have the say of whether to do it,” he said.
Khanna’s resolution would affirm that communities can ban data centers in residential areas, reject increases in electric bills and require data centers to use clean energy, among other provisions.

Data centers have cropped up across the country to support the rise in artificial intelligence, but the centers have created controversy in local communities, where residents have raised concerns over the centers’ water and energy consumption, noise and air pollution.
Now, candidates have had to grapple with data centers as an electoral issue. A March Gallup survey found that 71% of Americans somewhat or strongly opposed local construction of AI data centers.

title: Novak Djokovic reveals unspecified health issue after ouster at Cincinnati Open
summary: Tennis star Novak Djokovic alluded to a health condition after an early exit from the Cincinnati Open, in which he lost to 25-year-old Thiago Agustín Tirante in the second round.
story: Tennis star Novak Djokovic alluded to a health condition after an early exit from the Cincinnati Open on Saturday, in which he lost to 25-year-old Thiago Agustín Tirante in the second round.

Djokovic, 39, was visibly struggling throughout the match and appeared to vomit at one point, requiring a medical timeout. The match lasted nearly three hours before Tirante ultimately took down the 24-time Grand Slam champion.
It was “not an enjoyable” match, Djokovic told reporters after the loss.
“It’s just a condition that I have, healthwise, that has been bothering me for the past couple of years,” Djokovic said. “A lot of issues, especially when it is humid and it is hot.”
The Serbian star did not name or elaborate on the health issue. He had anticipated the humidity heading into the match but noted that other factors, including nerves, “make it worse.”

Djokovic congratulated Tirante after the match. Tirante, for his part, called the win potentially the best of his career and praised Djokovic as one of the most important figures the sport has ever seen.
“I think I really did a good job inside the court,” Tirante said. “I managed very well the nerves of playing against a legend like Novak.”
Djokovic saved 13 of the 15 break points he faced, but Tirante broke his serve in the ninth game of the final set and served out the match, winning 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 in 2 hours and 44 minutes.
Djokovic has long dominated at the Cincinnati Open, but Saturday’s loss dropped his record there to 45-13, according to the ATP Tour — and it may be his last appearance at the tournament.
Asked whether he’d return, Djokovic seemed uncertain.
“I certainly hope so, but it looks more likely not, unfortunately,” he said. “But let’s see what the future brings.”
This tournament was Djokovic’s first since his loss to Italy’s Jannik Sinner at Wimbledon in July.
He withdrew from the Canadian Open earlier this month, likely resting up ahead of the U.S. Open — the year’s final Grand Slam, which begins Aug. 30. Djokovic has won the title four times.

title: The best backpacks for kids, tested and reviewed
summary: Looking for the best backpack for kids? A mom tested 7 top-rated options for a month, from State to L.L.Bean, to find the most durable, spacious and kid-approved picks for elementary school.
story: My daughter starts kindergarten this fall, and if you’d told me a year ago that backpack shopping would send me down this much of a rabbit hole, I wouldn’t have believed you. But here we are. Between the endless folders, snacks, lunch box, water bottle, extra clothes and whatever “special item” she insists on bringing each day, I quickly realized not just any bag would do. I needed something that could actually hold everything, survive a full year of playground drop-offs and cafeteria spills, and — maybe most importantly — make her excited to walk through those doors on day one.

So I did what any slightly obsessive mom does: I polled every parent I know for their tried-and-true recommendations, then my daughter and I turned our living room into a full-blown backpack testing lab. We checked zippers, tested straps, packed them full and let her be the final judge on which ones actually felt good to wear. After weeks of trial and error (and a few strong five-year-old opinions), we landed on a list of backpacks that made the cut. Here are the best ones we found — the ones that are as practical for parents as they are exciting for kids.
State Kane Backpack

When I started asking other parents which backpack they swore by, one name came up again and again: State Bags. I’m talking multiple moms telling me their kid is on their fourth or fifth year with the same one, still going strong. That kind of loyalty is hard to ignore, so we had to try the brand for ourselves. Sized for ages 4 to 8 (K through 3rd grade), State’s Kane Backpack has a 15-liter capacity that swallowed up everything my daughter needed, with room to spare as she grows into bigger binders and books over the next few years. My daughter zeroed in on the metallic purple butterfly design immediately, and it’s still her favorite of everything we tested.

What sold me, though, was how practical it is underneath all that style. The main compartment fits folders, textbooks, and her sizeable lunchbox and snack box, while the interior is genuinely organized, with zip pockets, slip pockets, and pen holders so her stuff isn’t just floating around loose. My daughter could zip it herself with zero struggle, no sticking, no fighting with it, which matters a lot when you’re five and trying to be independent. The straps were just as easy: adjustable enough that we could cinch them down to actually fit her small frame, rather than the bag hanging off her. And when the inevitable spilled juice box or dropped snack happens, you can just wipe it down with a damp cloth and it looks brand new. Between the design she picked out herself and how easy the whole bag is for her to use on her own, it’s the one that made her genuinely excited. Also nice: the backpack comes in a mini size for kids ages 2-4 and a double-pocket style for kids over 7.
Calpak Miffy Kids Medium Backpack

The Calpak Miffy Kids Medium Backpack was an easy one to fall in love with. The Miffy Pink Zoo Trip print is genuinely cute and colorful without being overwhelming. Sized for ages 5 to 8, it holds 15 liters and one detail I didn’t expect to notice actually ended up really wowing me: the rounded square corners actually gave us more usable interior space than the traditional rounded-top backpacks we tried, so folders and books slid in without getting squeezed into an awkward curve.

My daughter also loved how comfortable the padded straps felt on her shoulders, even on days when the bag was packed full. And because she’s still pretty small, the adjustable sternum clip made a real difference. It kept the bag snug and centered on her frame instead of sliding around or pulling her backward, which is such a small thing but makes a big difference for a kid who’s still getting used to carrying her own stuff around all day.
The Children’s Place Girls Strawberry Backpack

I’ll admit, I wasn’t expecting much from a $16 backpack, but this bag pleasantly surprised me. It’s genuinely spacious for the price, with enough room for a lunch box alongside books, a pencil case, and the usual daily clutter, and the front-zip and side mesh pockets give her a place to stash smaller items separately. I also appreciated that it’s black, since it hides stains and scuffs far better than a lighter bag would, but it still has a fun strawberry print scattered across it that my daughter thought was “the cutest.” It doesn’t feel quite as sturdy or built-to-last as some of the pricier options on this list, but that’s to be expected at this price point, and for a budget pick or a backup bag, it more than holds its own.
L.L. Bean Original Book Pack

The L.L.Bean Original Book Pack is one of the roomiest options on this list, with a 24-liter capacity that easily fits a lunch box, books, worksheets and art projects with space to spare, but it never felt bulky or heavy on my daughter’s back. That’s because it’s made from a tough, weatherproof polyester that’s noticeably light while still standing up to daily wear, and it wipes down easily whenever it comes home a little worse for wear. My daughter was instantly drawn to the bold, bright print, since L.L.Bean offers a handful of really fun patterns to choose from, not just the classic solid colors. Beyond the look, it’s packed with practical details, like a key clip and organizer panel up front, a water bottle pocket, padded and reinforced shoulder straps, a padded back panel for comfort and reflective trim that gives me a little extra peace of mind for early mornings when the sun is still coming up.
Vineyard Vines Girls Metallic Backpack

My daughter is tall but slender, and a lot of the bags looked comically big on her. Not this one. It runs slightly smaller than the other options on the list, making it a good choice for younger kids.  Of everything we tested, it was the one that fit my daughter best, and given that she’s only five, that made a real difference in how comfortable and manageable it felt on her back rather than looking oversized or throwing off her balance. It has a fun metallic finish that adds a bit of shine without feeling over the top. And the pops of pink accents were delightful for my girlie girl daughter.
Simple Modern Fletcher Kids Backpack

I put the Simple Modern Fletcher Backpack to a real stress test during my daughter’s forest summer camp. Days spent traversing our local reservation meant she needed to haul more than the usual school-day essentials: sunscreen, bug spray, a hat, a full change of clothes, a snack, lunch and a water bottle, just to name a few. This is where the backpack’s interior organization really earned its keep. Between the large zip-closure front pocket, a separate zip-closure stash pocket, a padded tablet sleeve, and two expandable side sleeves for bottles, everything had its own designated spot. My daughter and I both loved that she could find what she needed without digging through one big jumbled compartment, which made those hectic camp mornings and pickups go so much smoother. I also appreciated how the adjustable straps and chest buckle kept it secure and comfortable on her small frame even when it was fully loaded down, and it held up well through a month of dirt, sunscreen smudges, and general outdoor chaos.

How I tested the best backpacks for kids

To find the best backpacks for kids, I enlisted my daughter as my official tester for a full month. We took each backpack through the paces of real life, from summer camp to play dates to everyday errands, so I could see how they actually held up. I focused specifically on backpacks appropriate for elementary school-aged kids, not middle or high schoolers, since their needs (and their strength) are pretty different. Here’s what I looked for:

Ease of use: A backpack is only as good as a kid’s ability to actually use it on their own. If she can’t get it on and off by herself, or if she’s fumbling with a stuck zipper while a line of classmates waits behind her, it’s not going to work. To test this, I loaded each backpack with the kind of stuff she’d realistically carry, like a lunchbox, water bottle and books, then had her put it on and take it off repeatedly. We also paid close attention to whether the zippers glided open and shut smoothly or tended to snag and stick.Durability: I wanted a backpack that could survive an entire school year, and ideally hold up for multiple years after that. I wanted something proportional to an elementary school kid’s frame, so it wasn’t so big that she’d topple over once it was loaded up, but not so small that it couldn’t comfortably hold a lunchbox, water bottle, snack and homework at the same time.
